ji-you.intro_tr: 既...又... [jì...yòu...] is a formal, written-style structure meaning "both...and..." It connects two adjectives, verbs, or verb phrases that describe the same subject, showing that two qualities or actions are equally true at the same time. The two parts linked by 既 and 又 must be grammatically parallel — both adjectives, both verbs, or both verb phrases of the same polarity. Compared to the everyday spoken pattern 又...又... [yòu...yòu...], 既...又... sounds more literary and is common in essays, reports, reviews, and formal speech. It typically links exactly two items and cannot be stretched to three without repeating 又 or switching structures.

tables.caption_tr: Core Structure: S + 既 + X + 又 + Y
rows: S + 既 + Adj1 + 又 + Adj2
他既聪明又努力。[Tā jì cōngmíng yòu nǔlì.]
He is both smart and hardworking.
S + 既 + V1 + 又 + V2
这个办法既省时又省力。[Zhège bànfǎ jì shěngshí yòu shěnglì.]
This method saves both time and effort.
S + 既 + 是 + N1 + 又 + 是 + N2
他既是老师又是我的朋友。[Tā jì shì lǎoshī yòu shì wǒ de péngyou.]
He is both a teacher and my friend.
S + 既 + VP1 + 又 + VP2 (verb phrases)
她既会说英语又会说法语。[Tā jì huì shuō Yīngyǔ yòu huì shuō Fǎyǔ.]
She can speak both English and French.
既 + Adj1 + 又 + Adj2 + 的 + N (modifier)
这是一个既经济又实用的方法。[Zhè shì yí ge jì jīngjì yòu shíyòng de fāngfǎ.]
This is a method that is both economical and practical.
footnotes_tr: 既 [jì] almost always comes right after the subject, not before it.
The two linked items must belong to the same word class (both adjectives, both verbs, etc.).

tables.caption_tr: 既...又... vs Related 'Both/And' Patterns
rows: Two qualities coexist equally, often complementary or used for praise
他既谦虚又努力。[Tā jì qiānxū yòu nǔlì.] — He is both modest and hardworking.
Simple everyday listing of two qualities or actions
这个包又便宜又好看。[Zhège bāo yòu piányi yòu hǎokàn.] — This bag is both cheap and nice-looking.
Almost identical to 既...又...; 也 feels a bit more additive/neutral
他既懂英语也懂日语。[Tā jì dǒng Yīngyǔ yě dǒng Rìyǔ.] — He knows both English and Japanese.
Progressive: the second point adds something stronger, not just parallel
他不但聪明而且勤奋。[Tā búdàn cōngmíng érqiě qínfèn.] — He is not only smart but also diligent.
他一边吃饭一边看电视。[Tā yìbiān chīfàn yìbiān kàn diànshì.] — He eats while watching TV.
footnotes_tr: Choose 既...又... over 又...又... when writing formally (essays, reports, news, speeches).

tables.caption_tr: Common Fixed Collocations with 既...又...
rows: 既高兴又激动 [jì gāoxìng yòu jīdòng]
既聪明又用功 [jì cōngmíng yòu yònggōng]
既方便又便宜 [jì fāngbiàn yòu piányi]
既经济又实用 [jì jīngjì yòu shíyòng]
既深刻又生动 [jì shēnkè yòu shēngdòng]
既紧张又兴奋 [jì jǐnzhāng yòu xīngfèn]
既安全又快捷 [jì ānquán yòu kuàijié]
既省时又省力 [jì shěngshí yòu shěnglì]

tables.caption_tr: Negative and Special Forms
rows: 他既不高也不矮。[Tā jì bù gāo yě bù ǎi.]
He is neither tall nor short.
这既非偶然又非巧合。[Zhè jì fēi ǒurán yòu fēi qiǎohé.]
This is neither coincidence nor accident.
他既聪明又努力，怎么会失败呢？[Tā jì cōngmíng yòu nǔlì, zěnme huì shībài ne?]
He's both smart and hardworking, so how could he fail?
footnotes_tr: In negative parallel structures, 也 [yě] is far more common than 又 [yòu] for the second clause.
既非...又非... belongs to very formal/literary registers (e.g. essays, legal or academic text).

tables.caption_tr: Common Mistakes
rows: *他既聪明又跑步很快。 (mixing adjective + verb phrase)
他既聪明又跑得快。[Tā jì cōngmíng yòu pǎo de kuài.]
The two linked items must be grammatically parallel — both adjectives or both verb-complement phrases, not mixed types.
*既他聪明又努力。 (既 placed before the subject)
他既聪明又努力。[Tā jì cōngmíng yòu nǔlì.]
既 [jì] normally follows the subject; unlike 虽然 [suīrán], it does not usually precede it.
*他既学习又工作又休息。 (three items strung together)
他既学习又工作，还要照顾家庭。[Tā jì xuéxí yòu gōngzuò, hái yào zhàogù jiātíng.]
既...又... links exactly two items; for three or more, add extra clauses with 还 [hái] or 并且 [bìngqiě] instead of repeating 又.
Using 既...又... in casual chatting
又便宜又好吃 [yòu piányi yòu hǎochī] (spoken version)
In everyday conversation, 又...又... sounds far more natural; 既...又... belongs mainly to writing and formal speech.

yaoshi-dehua.title_tr: Conditional Sentences: 要是 (yàoshi) and ...的话 (...dehuà)
yaoshi-dehua.intro_tr: Chinese expresses "if..." conditional sentences using a pair of clauses: a condition clause and a result clause, usually linked by 就[jiù] ("then") in the result clause. 要是[yàoshi] is the most common everyday, spoken word for "if," slightly more casual than 如果[rúguǒ]. The particle 的话[dehuà] ("if it's the case that...") can be attached to the end of the condition clause instead of, or together with, 要是/如果 — it is extremely common in spoken Chinese and can even stand alone after a bare statement to make it conditional. Word order is flexible: the condition clause can come with or without an explicit subject before 要是, and 的话 always sits at the very end of the condition clause, right before the comma. Mastering these patterns lets you sound natural instead of relying only on the more formal 如果...就....

tables.caption_tr: Core conditional markers compared
rows: most common in everyday conversation; slightly more casual than 如果
'if, supposing that'; often for hypothetical scenarios
similar to 假如, used in essays and formal speech
'were it the case that...'; found in written/literary style
classical-flavored 'if', used alone or in 若是
attached at the END of the condition clause; can replace or add to any of the above

tables.caption_tr: 要是 / 的话 sentence patterns
rows: 要是下雨，我们就不去。[Yàoshi xiàyǔ, wǒmen jiù bú qù.]
If it rains, we won't go.
下雨的话，我们就不去。[Xiàyǔ dehuà, wǒmen jiù bú qù.]
If it rains, we won't go.
要是 + condition + 的话, (就) + result
要是下雨的话，我们就不去。[Yàoshi xiàyǔ dehuà, wǒmen jiù bú qù.]
If it rains, we won't go. (most colloquial, most emphatic)
如果 + condition + 的话, (就) + result
如果你同意的话，就签字吧。[Rúguǒ nǐ tóngyì dehuà, jiù qiānzì ba.]
你要是不来，我就自己去。[Nǐ yàoshi bù lái, wǒ jiù zìjǐ qù.]
If you don't come, I'll go by myself.

tables.caption_tr: Word order and placement rules
rows: start of condition clause, OR right after the subject
你要是... = ...要是你... is NOT allowed; subject must precede 要是, not follow it
always at the very end of the condition clause, before the comma
never placed at the start of a clause
start of the result clause, right before the verb
optional but very common; omitting it is fine in short casual sentences
can be omitted if same as condition clause subject
要是你忙，(你)就先走吧。[Yàoshi nǐ máng, (nǐ) jiù xiān zǒu ba.]

tables.caption_tr: 要是/的话 vs. other common conditional patterns
rows: 要是有空，就给我打电话。[Yàoshi yǒu kòng, jiù gěi wǒ dǎ diànhuà.] — If you're free, call me.
neutral, slightly more formal/written than 要是
如果你努力，就会成功。[Rúguǒ nǐ nǔlì, jiù huì chénggōng.] — If you work hard, you'll succeed.
'as long as' — one sufficient condition guarantees result
只要你努力，就会成功。[Zhǐyào nǐ nǔlì, jiù huì chénggōng.] — As long as you work hard, you'll succeed.
'only if' — one necessary condition, no other way
只有努力，才能成功。[Zhǐyǒu nǔlì, cái néng chénggōng.] — Only by working hard can you succeed.
'even if' — result holds regardless of condition
即使下雨，我们也去。[Jíshǐ xiàyǔ, wǒmen yě qù.] — Even if it rains, we'll still go.
'in case, what if' — worries about a low-probability event
万一他不来怎么办？[Wànyī tā bù lái zěnme bàn?] — What if he doesn't come?

tables.caption_tr: Common mistakes to avoid
rows: 的话 can never start a clause; it must close the condition clause
下雨的话，... (NOT 的话下雨，...)
主语放在要是后面又重复
don't repeat the subject awkwardly around 要是
你要是不来 (NOT 要是你你不来)
忘记就而导致结果句意不清
dropping 就 in longer/complex sentences can make the result clause sound disconnected; keep 就 in anything but short casual remarks
要是你不同意，我们就取消计划。 (keep 就 here)
混用如果的话和要是的话为双重标记时语序错误
when combining, the order must be MARKER + condition + 的话, never 的话 + MARKER
要是他生病的话 (NOT 的话他生病要是)

yi-jiu.intro_tr: The pattern 一...就... [yī...jiù...] links two actions or events to show that the second happens immediately after the first — much like English "as soon as" or "once... then...". It can describe a one-time, specific sequence of events (often in the past, with 了) or a habitual, automatic reaction that happens every time the first condition occurs. The subject can be shared by both clauses (stated once, before 一) or different for each clause (stated separately before 一 and before 就). Because it emphasizes closeness in TIME between two events, it is easy to confuse with condition-focused patterns like 只要...就... and the more dramatic, formal 一旦...就.... This pattern is extremely frequent in everyday spoken Chinese as well as in narrative writing.

tables.caption_tr: Basic Structure of 一...就...
rows: 一 [yī] goes directly before the verb, not before the subject
就 [jiù] goes directly before the verb
"As soon as S1 does V1, S2 does V2"
Comma is optional; spoken Chinese often has a slight pause
footnotes_tr: 一 [yī] here is not the number 'one' — it functions as a time-sequencing marker meaning 'once / as soon as'.

tables.caption_tr: Same-Subject vs. Different-Subject Patterns
rows: S + 一 + V1, 就 + V2
我一到家就洗澡。 [Wǒ yī dào jiā jiù xǐzǎo.]
As soon as I get home, I take a shower.
S1 + 一 + V1, S2 + 就 + V2
老师一走,学生就说话。 [Lǎoshī yī zǒu, xuésheng jiù shuōhuà.]
As soon as the teacher leaves, the students talk.
一 + V1(+O), S + 就 + V2
一下课,他就回家。 [Yī xiàkè, tā jiù huí jiā.]
As soon as class ends, he goes home.

tables.caption_tr: Habitual Reaction vs. Specific One-Time Event
rows: no 了 [le] needed; reads as a general rule
他一累就想睡觉。 [Tā yī lèi jiù xiǎng shuìjiào.]
Whenever he's tired, he wants to sleep.
了 [le] usually appears after V2 (sometimes after both verbs)
我一到家就给她打了电话。 [Wǒ yī dào jiā jiù gěi tā dǎle diànhuà.]
As soon as I got home, I called her.
no 了 [le]; time words or context show future
明天你一到,我们就出发。 [Míngtiān nǐ yī dào, wǒmen jiù chūfā.]
Tomorrow, as soon as you arrive, we'll set off.
footnotes_tr: 了 [le] never attaches directly after 就 [jiù] — it attaches after the second verb (V2), e.g. 就打了电话, not 就了打电话.

tables.caption_tr: 一...就... vs. Related Conditional/Sequential Patterns
rows: as soon as / once (immediate time sequence)
Emphasizes that two events happen right after each other in TIME
他一到就笑了。 [Tā yī dào jiù xiào le.] — As soon as he arrived, he smiled.
More formal; implies a significant, often irreversible or hypothetical change
一旦你决定了,就不能改变。 [Yīdàn nǐ juédìng le, jiù bù néng gǎibiàn.] — Once you've decided, you can't change it.
Focuses on a sufficient CONDITION for a result, not on timing
只要你努力,就会成功。 [Zhǐyào nǐ nǔlì, jiù huì chénggōng.] — As long as you work hard, you'll succeed.
Just connects two clauses logically; no 'immediately' nuance
他累了就休息。 [Tā lèi le jiù xiūxi.] — He's tired, so he rests.

tables.caption_tr: Common Mistakes with 一...就...
rows: 了 [le] must attach directly after the verb (打了), never after 就
我一到家就打了电话。 [Wǒ yī dào jiā jiù dǎle diànhuà.]
一 [yī] must come after the subject in that clause, not before it
我一到家就洗澡。 [Wǒ yī dào jiā jiù xǐzǎo.]
一 in this pattern must be followed by a verb phrase, not just a noun
Use 一下雨 (verb 下), not 一雨
Dropping 就 in the second clause
就 [jiù] is obligatory — without it the pattern is broken
他一进门就笑了, not 他一进门,笑了

yushi-yinci.intro_tr: 于是[yúshì] and 因此[yīncǐ] both sit at the head of a second clause to link it to what came before, and both are often translated as "so" or "therefore" — but they express different kinds of connection. 于是[yúshì] signals a natural next step in a story: event A happened, and then B followed as a direct, chronological consequence ("thereupon, and so"). 因此[yīncǐ] signals a logical or reasoned cause-and-effect relationship, closer to formal "therefore, for this reason," and is common in written, explanatory, or argumentative text. Neither word needs a matching word in the first clause (unlike 因为...所以...[yīnwèi...suǒyǐ...]), and both always start the second clause, never the first.

tables.caption_tr: 于是[yúshì] vs 因此[yīncǐ]: core differences
rows: 'thereupon, and so' — a natural next step
'therefore, for this reason' — a logical conclusion
Neutral, very common in spoken and written narration
More formal, typical of written/explanatory text
Rare — 于是[yúshì] usually stands alone, not paired
Yes, often used after 因为[yīnwèi]... clauses
Can be replaced by 所以[suǒyǐ]?
Often yes, but loses the 'and then' narrative flavor
Yes, 因此[yīncǐ] is more formal than 所以[suǒyǐ]
Always starts clause 2 (before or after subject)
Always starts clause 2 (before or after subject)

tables.caption_tr: Sentence patterns
rows: Tā hěn lèi, yúshì zǎozǎo shuì le.
He was tired, so he went to bed early.
天气不好，因此比赛推迟了。
Tiānqì bù hǎo, yīncǐ bǐsài tuīchí le.
The weather was bad, so the match was postponed.
因为下雪，因此航班取消了。
Yīnwèi xià xuě, yīncǐ hángbān qǔxiāo le.
Because it snowed, the flight was cancelled.
他很守时，也因此赢得了大家的尊重。
Tā hěn shǒushí, yě yīncǐ yíngdéle dàjiā de zūnzhòng.
He is very punctual, and for this reason too he earned everyone's respect.

tables.caption_tr: 于是[yúshì] / 因此[yīncǐ] compared with similar connectors
rows: 'and then' — next event in a sequence
'so' — general result, usually paired with 因为
'thus, hence' — very close to 因此, slightly more literary
'thereby' — result achieved through a method or action
'as a result' — often an unexpected or final outcome

tables.caption_tr: Common fixed expressions and collocations
rows: Old-fashioned or humorous flourish of 于是
Links 因此 directly to a following verb phrase
Adds another consequence to a list
就 adds immediacy to the sequence

tables.caption_tr: Common mistakes
rows: Yīnwèi hěn lèi, yúshì tā shuì le.
于是 rarely pairs naturally with 因为; sounds unnatural
因为很累，所以他睡了 / 他很累，于是睡了
于是 must introduce a RESULT, not a state with no preceding cause
Add a cause first: 他工作到很晚，于是很累。
于是 and 因此 cannot be stacked together
Choose only one: 于是他走了 / 因此他走了
Using 因此 to open a spoken casual chat sentence with no clear logic
因此 sounds stiff/overly formal in casual speech
Use 所以[suǒyǐ] or 于是[yúshì] in everyday conversation

lian-dou.intro_tr: 连...都/也 (lián...dōu/yě) is a structure used to emphasize an extreme example, meaning "even X" — it implies that if even this extreme case is true, then everything less extreme must be true as well. It is especially common in negative sentences to express "not even X," pointing out that even the smallest, easiest, or most basic threshold was not met. The word 连[lián] introduces the item being emphasized (a person, thing, quantity, or action), and 都[dōu] or 也[yě] follows it to complete the structure — the two are largely interchangeable, with 都 being more common in everyday speech. This pattern carries strong emotional emphasis and is extremely frequent in spoken Chinese, roughly matching English "even" or "not even" in tone.

tables.caption_tr: Core structure of 连...都/也
rows: "Even" — placed directly before the item being emphasized
X (noun / pronoun / number+measure word / verb phrase)
The extreme case being singled out — the smallest, easiest, or least likely example
Required adverb that completes the structure; 都 is more common in speech, 也 is slightly more formal/literary — usually interchangeable
The main predicate; frequently negated to mean "not even...", but can also be affirmative

tables.caption_tr: Affirmative vs. negative patterns
rows: 连小孩都懂[lián xiǎohái dōu dǒng] — "Even a child understands"
连 + X + 都/也 + 不/没 + V
"Not even X does/is V" (negative emphasis, most common)
连他都不知道[lián tā dōu bù zhīdào] — "Even he doesn't know"
连 + Number+Measure Word + 都/也 + 没有
连一分钱都没有[lián yì fēn qián dōu méiyǒu] — "Don't even have a single cent"
连 + V + 都/也 + 没 + V
"Didn't even V" (verb repeated to show it never happened)
连问都没问[lián wèn dōu méi wèn] — "Didn't even ask"

tables.caption_tr: Common fixed expressions with 连
rows: didn't even step out the door

tables.caption_tr: 连...都/也 compared to similar "even" structures
rows: Neutral, most common way to say "even"
连他都来了[lián tā dōu láile] — "Even he came"
Default choice; works in speech and writing
"Even, to the point that" — can introduce a whole clause
他甚至不吃饭[tā shènzhì bù chīfàn] — "He even doesn't eat"
Can combine with 连: 甚至连...都
"Even" with extra emphasis, often formal or written
就连老师也不懂[jiùlián lǎoshī yě bù dǒng] — "Even the teacher doesn't understand"
就 intensifies 连; often sentence-initial
Weaker, general emphasis without the "even" nuance
谁都知道[shéi dōu zhīdào] — "Everyone knows"
Used with question words like 谁/什么 for "everyone/everything", not a true "even" statement

tables.caption_tr: Common mistakes
rows: 都 or 也 is required to complete the structure — 连 alone cannot stand without it
连 must be placed directly before the emphasized item (这件事), not separated from it
When emphasizing an absence/minimum, the verb phrase after 都/也 usually needs negation (没有/不)
连我也去了很高兴 (✗, unclear)
Keep the structure tight: 连 + X + 都/也 + short verb phrase; avoid burying the emphasized item in a long clause

nandao-rhetorical.title_tr: 难道[nándào]: Rhetorical Question 'Don't Tell Me...?' / 'Surely Not...?'
nandao-rhetorical.intro_tr: 难道[nándào] is an adverb that turns an ordinary statement into a rhetorical question — a question that isn't really asking for new information, but is used to push the listener toward a conclusion the speaker already believes is true. It corresponds to English phrases like "Don't tell me...?", "Could it be that...?", or "Surely...?". 难道 almost always pairs with a sentence-final question marker such as 吗[ma] or the more forceful 不成[bùchéng]. The single most important trick to master is the "meaning flip": a 难道 sentence that looks grammatically positive actually asserts a negative truth, and one that looks negative actually asserts a positive truth. Because it is rhetorical, 难道 should never be used when you genuinely want to ask for unknown information — for that, use plain questions or 到底[dàodǐ]/究竟[jiūjìng] instead.

tables.caption_tr: Basic Sentence Patterns with 难道[nándào]
rows: 难道你不爱我吗?[Nándào nǐ bú ài wǒ ma?]
Don't you love me? (= You must love me)
你难道不爱我吗?[Nǐ nándào bú ài wǒ ma?]
subject placed before 难道, same meaning
Identical meaning to the pattern above; slightly less dramatic
难道 + S + V(+O) + 不成?
难道他不来了不成?[Nándào tā bù lái le bùchéng?]
'不成' = 'is that not so?', colloquial and blunt
难道说他忘了?[Nándào shuō tā wàng le?]
Softer, conversational way to introduce a rhetorical guess
footnotes_tr: 难道 can stand either before or after the subject with no change in core meaning; placing it at the very start of the sentence often feels slightly more dramatic.
难道 questions are almost never answered literally with 是/不是 — they function as emphatic statements, not real requests for information.

tables.caption_tr: The 'Meaning Flip': Positive Surface Form vs Negative Surface Form
rows: NO — the speaker is denying it / expressing disbelief
难道你是傻子吗?[Nándào nǐ shì shǎzi ma?] → 'You're not an idiot, are you?!' (implies: 你不是傻子, you are clearly not)
难道 + negative verb (不/没) + 吗?
YES — the speaker is asserting it strongly
难道你不知道吗?[Nándào nǐ bù zhīdào ma?] → implies 你应该知道, 'You definitely should know!'
footnotes_tr: This flip is the single hardest part of 难道 for beginners: read the surface grammar, then mentally reverse it to get the speaker's true point.

tables.caption_tr: Common Collocations and Variants of 难道
rows: The standard, most common rhetorical-question frame
难道这不是真的吗?[Nándào zhè bú shì zhēn de ma?] — 'Isn't this true?'
Colloquial, extra emphatic, mostly spoken register
难道你还想赖账不成?[Nándào nǐ hái xiǎng làizhàng bùchéng?] — 'Don't tell me you still want to skip out on the bill?!'
Softer, more tentative — introduces a surprised guess
难道说他生病了?[Nándào shuō tā shēngbìng le?] — 'Could it be that he's sick?'
难道就没有办法了吗?[Nándào jiù méiyǒu bànfǎ le ma?] — 'Is there really no way at all?'

tables.caption_tr: 难道 vs Similar Rhetorical/Doubt Markers
rows: General-purpose rhetorical doubt or emphatic assertion
难道你不怕吗?[Nándào nǐ bú pà ma?]
Formal written register, 'how could it possibly be that...'
岂能如此?[Qǐ néng rúcǐ?] — 'How could this possibly be so?'
Expresses a worried guess, softer/less confident than 难道
他不会不来吧?[Tā bú huì bù lái ba?] — 'He won't not come, will he?'
A genuine information-seeking question, NOT rhetorical
你到底去不去?[Nǐ dàodǐ qù bu qù?] — 'Are you going or not, exactly?'
footnotes_tr: 到底/究竟 truly wants an answer; 难道 already assumes the answer and uses the question only for rhetorical effect — do not confuse the two.

tables.caption_tr: Common Mistakes with 难道
rows: Using 难道 to ask a genuine, information-seeking question
难道 is rhetorical only — it cannot be used when you truly don't know the answer
Use a plain question or 到底/究竟 instead: 你到底去不去?[Nǐ dàodǐ qù bu qù?]
Dropping the sentence-final 吗/不成 while still expecting rhetorical force
难道 almost always needs 吗, 不成, or clearly rhetorical intonation to complete the pattern
难道你不知道 → 难道你不知道吗?[Nándào nǐ bù zhīdào ma?]
Interpreting a 难道 sentence literally instead of applying the meaning flip
Learners often answer as if the surface grammar were the real meaning
Remember: 难道+affirmative = rhetorical NO; 难道+negative = rhetorical YES
Placing 难道 mid-clause after other adverbs like 已经/也
难道 should come at the very start of the clause or right after the subject, not buried after other adverbs
难道你已经忘了吗? (✓) rather than 你已经难道忘了吗? (✗)

examples.target: 难道你不认识我了吗?
examples.reading: Nándào nǐ bú rènshi wǒ le ma?
examples.translation_tr: Don't tell me you don't recognize me anymore? (i.e., you surely still know who I am)

examples.target: 这么晚了,难道他还没到家吗?
examples.reading: Zhème wǎn le, nándào tā hái méi dào jiā ma?
examples.translation_tr: It's so late — could it really be that he still hasn't gotten home?

examples.reading: Nándào wǒmen jiù zhèyàng fàngqì ma?

examples.translation_tr: Don't tell me you forgot today is my birthday?!

shenzhi.intro_tr: 甚至[shènzhì] is an adverb meaning "even" or "to the extent that," used to spotlight the most extreme, surprising, or unexpected item in a list, or to introduce a whole clause that goes beyond what was already stated. It signals that if this extreme case holds true, everything mentioned before it is naturally true as well. 甚至 very often pairs with 都[dōu] or 也[yě] right before the verb for extra emphasis, and it can combine with 连[lián] (甚至连...都/也...) for the strongest possible "even" statement. Unlike 连...都/也 alone, which can only mark a single item, 甚至 is flexible enough to link separate words, phrases, or entire sentences. Its more literary cousin 甚至于[shènzhìyú] appears mainly in formal writing.

tables.caption_tr: Core Sentence Patterns with 甚至[shènzhì]
rows: Last item in a list is the most extreme/surprising one
他会做饭、洗衣服，甚至打扫房间。[Tā huì zuò fàn, xǐ yīfu, shènzhì dǎsǎo fángjiān.]
He can cook, do laundry, and even clean the house.
Whole clause added as an extreme extra fact
他忘记了很多事，甚至忘记了自己的生日。[Tā wàngjìle hěn duō shì, shènzhì wàngjìle zìjǐ de shēngrì.]
He forgot many things — he even forgot his own birthday.
甚至[shènzhì] + Subject + 都/也[dōu/yě] + V
Emphasize a surprising subject with 都/也
这件事甚至老师都不知道。[Zhè jiàn shì shènzhì lǎoshī dōu bù zhīdào.]
Even the teacher doesn't know about this matter.
甚至连[shènzhì lián] + N + 都/也[dōu/yě] + V
Strongest emphasis, combines 甚至 and 连
他甚至连自己的名字都写错了。[Tā shènzhì lián zìjǐ de míngzi dōu xiěcuò le.]
He even got his own name wrong.
他从不休息，甚至于生病也照常上班。[Tā cóng bù xiūxi, shènzhìyú shēngbìng yě zhàocháng shàngbān.]
He never rests; he even goes to work as usual when sick.

tables.caption_tr: 甚至[shènzhì] vs 连[lián]...都/也 vs Combined Form
rows: Marks one single extreme item inside a clause; 都/也 is required
他连一个字都不认识。[Tā lián yí ge zì dōu bú rènshi.]
Cannot link a whole list or a separate clause, only one item within the same clause
Introduces the most extreme item in a list or an extreme extra clause; 都/也 optional
他连一个字都不认识，甚至自己的名字也写不出来。[Tā lián yí ge zì dōu bú rènshi, shènzhì zìjǐ de míngzi yě xiě bu chūlái.]
More flexible; can add a full new clause after other items
他甚至连一个字都不认识。[Tā shènzhì lián yí ge zì dōu bú rènshi.]
Very common in speech; strongest 'even' emphasis

tables.caption_tr: Position of 甚至[shènzhì] in the Sentence
rows: 甚至我自己也不相信这是真的。[Shènzhì wǒ zìjǐ yě bù xiāngxìn zhè shì zhēn de.]
Even I myself don't believe this is true. (whole clause, subject included, is the extreme case)
我甚至都不相信这是真的。[Wǒ shènzhì dōu bù xiāngxìn zhè shì zhēn de.]
I don't even believe this is true. (subject is known/background; predicate is the extreme part)
他吃了很多东西，甚至一整只鸡。[Tā chīle hěn duō dōngxi, shènzhì yì zhěng zhī jī.]
He ate a lot of things, even a whole chicken.

tables.caption_tr: Formal and Extended Forms of 甚至[shènzhì]
rows: More literary/written; interchangeable with 甚至
这个计划太复杂，甚至于连专家都看不懂。[Zhège jìhuà tài fùzá, shènzhìyú lián zhuānjiā dōu kàn bu dǒng.]
Used right before a noun phrase, 'or even'
他对每个人都很客气，甚至是陌生人。[Tā duì měi ge rén dōu hěn kèqi, shènzhì shì mòshēngrén.]
'one could even say that...', introduces a bold claim
这本书写得很好，甚至可以说是今年最好的小说。[Zhè běn shū xiě de hěn hǎo, shènzhì kěyǐ shuō shì jīnnián zuì hǎo de xiǎoshuō.]

tables.caption_tr: Common Mistakes with 甚至[shènzhì]
rows: 他甚至连饭都忘了吃。[Tā shènzhì lián fàn dōu wàngle chī.]
When 甚至 combines with 连, 都 or 也 is required right before the verb.
Placing 甚至 after the extreme item
他甚至不知道这件事。[Tā shènzhì bù zhīdào zhè jiàn shì.]
甚至 must come before the item or clause it emphasizes, never after it.
Using 甚至 for an ordinary, non-extreme list item
我喜欢苹果、香蕉，甚至葡萄。 (*, all equally common fruits)
我喜欢苹果、香蕉，甚至榴莲。[Wǒ xǐhuan píngguǒ, xiāngjiāo, shènzhì liúlián.]
The item after 甚至 must be genuinely more extreme, surprising, or unusual than the others — durian is a strong/unexpected example, unlike grapes.
Treating 甚至是 and 甚至 as always interchangeable
他很喜欢运动，甚至是陌生人。 (*, awkward without noun focus)
他对每个人都很客气，甚至是陌生人。[Tā duì měi ge rén dōu hěn kèqi, shènzhì shì mòshēngrén.]
甚至是 specifically introduces a noun phrase as the extreme example; use plain 甚至 before verbs/clauses.

examples.target: 他每天工作十几个小时，甚至周末也不休息。
examples.reading: Tā měitiān gōngzuò shí jǐ ge xiǎoshí, shènzhì zhōumò yě bù xiūxi.
examples.translation_tr: He works more than ten hours every day, and doesn't even rest on weekends.

examples.target: 这个消息太意外了，甚至连总统都感到吃惊。
examples.reading: Zhège xiāoxi tài yìwài le, shènzhì lián zǒngtǒng dōu gǎndào chījīng.
examples.translation_tr: The news was so unexpected that even the president was surprised.

examples.target: 她的中文说得很好，甚至比很多中国人说得还标准。
examples.reading: Tā de Zhōngwén shuō de hěn hǎo, shènzhì bǐ hěn duō Zhōngguórén shuō de hái biāozhǔn.
examples.translation_tr: Her Chinese is so good that she even speaks more standard than many native speakers.

examples.target: 天气冷极了，甚至下起了雪。
examples.reading: Tiānqì lěng jí le, shènzhì xiàqǐle xuě.
examples.translation_tr: It was extremely cold — it even started snowing.

examples.target: 我甚至不记得昨天晚上吃了什么。
examples.reading: Wǒ shènzhì bú jìde zuótiān wǎnshang chīle shénme.
examples.translation_tr: I don't even remember what I ate last night.

examples.target: 他对这份工作很不满意，甚至想辞职。
examples.reading: Tā duì zhè fèn gōngzuò hěn bù mǎnyì, shènzhì xiǎng cízhí.
examples.translation_tr: He is very unhappy with this job — he's even thinking about quitting.

examples.target: 甚至连小孩子都懂这个道理。
examples.reading: Shènzhì lián xiǎoháizi dōu dǒng zhège dàolǐ.
examples.translation_tr: Even little children understand this principle.

que-contrast.title_tr: 却 (què): Contrast That Breaks Expectations — "but, yet, however"
que-contrast.intro_tr: 却 [què] is an adverb meaning "but, yet, however" that signals a result or fact contrary to what was expected. Unlike English "but," 却 never sits at the very front of a sentence or clause — it must be placed right after the subject/topic and before the verb or adjective, functioning like an inner adverb (similar to 也 or 都) rather than a connecting conjunction like 但是 or 可是. Because of this, 却 is very often paired with a leading conjunction such as 虽然 or 但 for extra emphasis, but it can also appear alone in the second half of a two-clause sentence to quietly mark a twist. Mastering 却 mainly means mastering its strict word-order rule, since that is where zero-level learners make the most mistakes.

tables.caption_tr: Basic word order with 却 [què]
rows: 他却不知道。 [Tā què bù zhīdào.]
却 must follow the subject; it cannot come before it.
我说了,他却没听。 [Wǒ shuōle, tā què méi tīng.]
却 is placed before 不/没, never after.
他很努力,结果却失败了。 [Tā hěn nǔlì, jiéguǒ què shībài le.]
却 marks the surprising or contrasting second half.

tables.caption_tr: Comparing 却 with other contrast words
rows: 他很累,但是他没有休息。 [Tā hěn lèi, dànshì tā méiyǒu xiūxi.]
我想去,可是没有时间。 [Wǒ xiǎng qù, kěshì méiyǒu shíjiān.]
还可以,不过有点儿贵。 [Hái kěyǐ, búguò yǒudiǎnr guì.]
No — cannot stand alone at the start
他很累,却不休息。 [Tā hěn lèi, què bù xiūxi.]

tables.caption_tr: Common combined patterns with 却
rows: 虽然很累,他却不休息。 [Suīrán hěn lèi, tā què bù xiūxi.]
我想去,但时间却不够。 [Wǒ xiǎng qù, dàn shíjiān què búgòu.]
他没上过学,却也懂不少道理。 [Tā méi shàngguo xué, què yě dǒng bùshǎo dàolǐ.]
yet again / on top of that
想帮忙,却又不知道怎么做。 [Xiǎng bāngmáng, què yòu bù zhīdào zěnme zuò.]

tables.caption_tr: Common mistakes with 却
rows: 却 must follow the subject, not precede it, since it is an adverb, not a sentence-initial conjunction.
❌ 却,他没有来。 (used to open a sentence like 但是)
✅ 他却没有来。 / 但是他没有来。
却 cannot stand alone at the very start of a sentence the way 但是/可是 can.
却 must be placed before the predicate (verb/adjective), never after it.

tables.caption_tr: Typical nuances carried by 却
rows: Marks a result that goes against what was expected
他复习了很久,却没考好。 [Tā fùxíle hěn jiǔ, què méi kǎohǎo.]
Simply highlights a difference, without strong surprise
妹妹喜欢红色,姐姐却喜欢蓝色。 [Mèimei xǐhuan hóngsè, jiějie què xǐhuan lánsè.]
Can carry a subtle tone of dissatisfaction
我帮了他,他却不感谢我。 [Wǒ bāngle tā, tā què bù gǎnxiè wǒ.]

examples.target: 他很聪明,学习成绩却不好。
examples.reading: Tā hěn cōngmíng, xuéxí chéngjì què bù hǎo.
examples.translation_tr: He's very smart, but his grades are not good.

examples.target: 我打了好几次电话,他却不接。
examples.reading: Wǒ dǎle hǎo jǐ cì diànhuà, tā què bù jiē.
examples.translation_tr: I called several times, but he wouldn't pick up.

examples.target: 虽然外面下雨,他却不带伞。
examples.reading: Suīrán wàimiàn xiàyǔ, tā què bú dài sǎn.
examples.translation_tr: Although it's raining outside, he doesn't bring an umbrella.

examples.target: 这个问题看起来很简单,做起来却很难。
examples.reading: Zhège wèntí kànqǐlai hěn jiǎndān, zuò qǐlai què hěn nán.
examples.translation_tr: This problem looks simple, but turns out to be very hard to actually do.

examples.target: 他年纪不大,知道的却很多。
examples.reading: Tā niánjì bú dà, zhīdào de què hěn duō.
examples.translation_tr: He isn't old, yet he knows a great deal.

examples.target: 大家都反对,他却坚持自己的想法。
examples.reading: Dàjiā dōu fǎnduì, tā què jiānchí zìjǐ de xiǎngfǎ.
examples.translation_tr: Everyone objected, but he insisted on his own idea anyway.

examples.target: 我帮了他那么多次,他却从来不感谢我。
examples.reading: Wǒ bāngle tā nàme duō cì, tā què cónglái bù gǎnxiè wǒ.
examples.translation_tr: I've helped him so many times, yet he never thanks me.

buru-comparison.title_tr: 不如 / 没有...那么 (Negative Comparison: "not as ... as")
buru-comparison.intro_tr: Mandarin has two common ways to say "A is not as [adjective] as B," and both are the mirror image of the 比 (bǐ) comparison you already know. The pattern 没有...那么/这么 literally says "A does not have B's such degree of [adjective]," and is the neutral, everyday way to state that one thing falls short of another in some quality. The pattern A不如B (+ adjective, optional) means "A is not equal to / falls short of B," and is often used more broadly to judge overall quality or to recommend B as the better choice — sometimes with the adjective dropped entirely. Unlike 没有...那么, 不如 never takes 那么/这么, and it commonly appears in the fixed pattern 与其...不如... ("rather than..., it's better to..."). Choose 没有...那么 for concrete degree comparisons (height, price, speed) in casual speech, and 不如 when comparing overall preferability or suggesting an alternative.

tables.caption_tr: Two Core Patterns for Negative Comparison
rows: A + 没有 + B + (那么/这么) + Adjective/Verb Phrase
A does not have B's such degree of [Adjective]
A is not as [Adjective] as B — the neutral, most common everyday form
A + 不如 + B + (Adjective/Verb Phrase, optional)
A is not equal to / falls short of B
A is inferior to B; often used to judge overall quality or recommend B as the better option

tables.caption_tr: Side-by-Side: Same Idea in Four Comparison Structures
rows: He is as tall as me.
He is not as tall as me.
He is not as tall as me (more natural for abilities/overall quality than for simple physical traits).

tables.caption_tr: 没有...那么 vs 不如: Key Differences
rows: Neutral, very common in casual speech
Slightly more evaluative, often implies a judgment or a suggestion
Yes — the adjective/verb phrase is usually stated
Optional — can be dropped, meaning simply 'A is not as good as B'
Can mean 'might as well do B instead'?
Yes — 不如 alone can mean 'it would be better to...'
Does it take 那么/这么?
Yes (那么 for distant/general reference, 这么 for close/immediate reference)
No — 不如 never combines with 那么/这么
Comparing the degree of a specific quality (height, price, speed, difficulty...)
Comparing overall quality/preferability, or recommending an alternative course of action

tables.caption_tr: Common Fixed Expressions Built on 不如
rows: rather than..., it would be better to...
与其等他,不如自己去。[Yǔqí děng tā, bùrú zìjǐ qù.] — 'Rather than waiting for him, it's better to go yourself.'
rather / it would be more accurate to say
这不是建议,不如说是命令。[Zhè bú shì jiànyì, bùrú shuō shì mìnglìng.] — 'This isn't a suggestion, it's more like an order.'
不如就今天出发吧。[Bùrú jiù jīntiān chūfā ba.] — 'How about we just leave today.'
far inferior to, nowhere near as good as
他的水平远不如你。[Tā de shuǐpíng yuǎn bùrú nǐ.] — 'His level is nowhere near as good as yours.'

tables.caption_tr: Common Mistakes to Avoid
rows: 他没有我那么高。 / 他不如我高。
Do not combine 没有 with 比 in the same clause — pick one negative-comparison pattern, not a mix of both.
不如 never takes 那么/这么; that marker belongs only to the 没有...那么 pattern.
那么/这么 must sit directly before the adjective, never after it.
这个不如那个好。 / 这个没有那个好。
Don't add a second negation (不好) after 不如 — 不如 already carries the negative meaning by itself.

examples.target: 我的中文没有他那么好。
examples.reading: Wǒ de Zhōngwén méiyǒu tā nàme hǎo.
examples.translation_tr: My Chinese is not as good as his.
examples.note_tr: Basic 没有...那么 pattern: A + 没有 + B + 那么 + Adjective.

examples.target: 这件衣服没有那件那么贵。
examples.reading: Zhè jiàn yīfu méiyǒu nà jiàn nàme guì.
examples.translation_tr: This piece of clothing is not as expensive as that one.

examples.target: 坐火车不如坐飞机快。
examples.reading: Zuò huǒchē bùrú zuò fēijī kuài.
examples.translation_tr: Taking the train is not as fast as taking the plane.
examples.note_tr: 不如 compares two verb phrases (坐火车 vs 坐飞机) directly, no 那么 needed.

examples.target: 今天不如昨天热。
examples.reading: Jīntiān bùrú zuótiān rè.
examples.translation_tr: Today is not as hot as yesterday.

examples.target: 与其在家看电视,不如出去运动。
examples.reading: Yǔqí zài jiā kàn diànshì, bùrú chūqù yùndòng.
examples.translation_tr: Rather than staying home watching TV, it would be better to go out and exercise.
examples.note_tr: 与其...不如... pairs a rejected option with a preferred one; 不如 here means 'it's better to'.

examples.target: 他跑得没有我这么快。
examples.reading: Tā pǎo de méiyǒu wǒ zhème kuài.
examples.translation_tr: He doesn't run as fast as I do.
examples.note_tr: 这么 is used instead of 那么 when the speaker treats the reference (我, 'me') as close/immediate.

examples.target: 我觉得这个方法不如那个方法好用。
examples.reading: Wǒ juéde zhège fāngfǎ bùrú nàge fāngfǎ hǎoyòng.
examples.translation_tr: I think this method isn't as useful as that one.

examples.target: 我们班的人数没有你们班那么多。
examples.reading: Wǒmen bān de rénshù méiyǒu nǐmen bān nàme duō.
examples.translation_tr: Our class doesn't have as many people as your class.

haoxiang-sihu.title_tr: 好像 / 似乎 ('seem, as if, appear to')
haoxiang-sihu.intro_tr: 好像[hǎoxiàng] and 似乎[sìhū] both translate as "seem, appear, as if" and are used to soften a statement into a guess, impression, or tentative judgment rather than a hard fact. 好像[hǎoxiàng] is the everyday, spoken-language choice and often pairs with 一样[yíyàng] or 似的[shìde] to build "as if... / just like..." comparisons. 似乎[sìhū] is more formal and literary, common in writing, news, and careful speech, and it rarely needs 一样/似的 to sound complete. Both words sit right before the verb phrase (after the subject) and can be negated by putting 不[bù] or 没[méi] inside the following clause. Because they mark a subjective impression, they are frequently combined with other hedging words such as 可能[kěnéng] 'probably' or 有点儿[yǒudiǎnr] 'a bit' for extra softness.

tables.caption_tr: 好像[hǎoxiàng] vs 似乎[sìhū]: register and usage comparison
rows: spoken / informal, used constantly in daily conversation
written / formal, common in essays, news, careful speech
often followed by 一样[yíyàng] or 似的[shìde] to complete the comparison
usually stands alone, rarely needs 一样/似的
less common, subject is usually stated
yes, especially in writing: 似乎有点儿冷。 (It seems a bit cold.)
often a direct sensory impression (sight, sound, feeling)
often a logical inference or deduction from evidence
好像...一样/似的 (doubling the 'as if' feeling)
not usually doubled; stands as a single hedging adverb
very natural: 好像要下雨了。
also fine but slightly more formal-sounding: 似乎要下雨了。

tables.caption_tr: Core sentence patterns with 好像 / 似乎
rows: Subject + 好像/似乎 + Verb Phrase
Subject + 好像/似乎 + 是 + Noun
那个人好像是我的老师。
That person seems to be my teacher.
好像/似乎 + whole clause (no clear subject, impersonal impression)
It looks like it's going to rain.
Subject + 好像/似乎 + 不/没 + Verb Phrase (negation)
He doesn't seem to recognize me.
Subject + 好像/似乎 + Clause + 一样/似的
他好像什么都不知道一样。
He acts as if he knows nothing.
好像/似乎 + 可能/有点儿 + Verb Phrase (double hedge)

tables.caption_tr: Fixed comparison structures: 好像...一样 / 似的 / 似乎...一般
rows: 他好像认识我一样,跟我打招呼。
He greeted me as if he knew me.
她好像哭过似的,眼睛红红的。
Her eyes were red, as if she had been crying.
Everything around seemed to have frozen still.
跟 + Noun/Clause + 一样 combined with 好像 for extra emphasis
今天好像跟平时不太一样。
Today seems a bit different from usual.

tables.caption_tr: 好像 / 似乎 vs similar 'seem, like' words
rows: means 'to resemble/be like'; needs a comparison object, not a full guess about a fact
everyday hedge for an impression or guess
hedge based on inference or reasoning
poetic, dreamlike 'as if'; stronger literary flavor than 似乎
based specifically on visual appearance: 'looking at it, it seems...'
almost identical to 看起来, slightly more common in southern/Taiwan Mandarin

tables.caption_tr: Common mistakes
rows: 像 alone cannot mean 'seem to'; use 好像 or 似乎 for a guess about a fact.
一样/似的 must attach directly to the end of the clause it completes, not form a separate sentence.
他似乎不高兴。 / 似乎他不太高兴,大家都很担心。
似乎 is more natural right after the subject; placing it before the subject is only acceptable in specific literary/topic-fronting contexts.
Avoid stacking unnecessary double negatives with 好像; keep the negation simple inside the following clause.
她好像很高兴的样子的样子。
Don't combine 好像 with a redundant repeated 的样子; choose one hedging device, not both stacked twice.

examples.target: 他好像感冒了。
examples.reading: tā hǎoxiàng gǎnmào le.
examples.translation_tr: He seems to have caught a cold.

examples.target: 天好像要下雨了。
examples.reading: tiān hǎoxiàng yào xià yǔ le.
examples.translation_tr: It looks like it's going to rain.

examples.target: 她似乎不太高兴。
examples.reading: tā sìhū bú tài gāoxìng.
examples.translation_tr: She doesn't seem very happy.

examples.target: 这件事好像跟他没关系。
examples.reading: zhè jiàn shì hǎoxiàng gēn tā méi guānxi.
examples.translation_tr: This matter seems to have nothing to do with him.

examples.target: 他好像没听懂似的,又问了一遍。
examples.reading: tā hǎoxiàng méi tīngdǒng shìde, yòu wènle yí biàn.

gang-vs-gangcai.title_tr: 刚 (gāng) vs 刚才 (gāngcái): The Difference Between Two Words for "Just Now"
gang-vs-gangcai.intro_tr: 刚[gāng] and 刚才[gāngcái] both translate as "just" or "a moment ago," but they belong to different word classes and cannot always be swapped. 刚[gāng] is an adverb that must sit directly in front of a verb and can never stand alone. 刚才[gāngcái] is a time noun that behaves like other time words (今天, 现在) — it can appear before or after the subject, can be modified by 的, and can even answer a question by itself. Because 刚才[gāngcái] is a noun, it also has a stricter time range: it only points to a few minutes ago within the same conversation or day, while 刚[gāng] can flexibly describe "just happened" over a slightly wider recent window. Getting the word class right is the key to using each one correctly.

tables.caption_tr: Core comparison: 刚[gāng] (adverb) vs 刚才[gāngcái] (time noun)
rows: Must sit directly before the verb
Flexible — before the subject or between subject and verb, like 今天[jīntiān] or 现在[xiànzài]
Can stand alone (e.g. as a one-word answer)
No — always needs a following verb
Yes: 你什么时候走的？——刚才。[Nǐ shénme shíhou zǒu de? — Gāngcái.]
Can take 的[de] to modify a noun
Yes: 刚才的事[gāngcái de shì] 'the matter from just now'
Yes: 这是刚才的电话。[Zhè shì gāngcái de diànhuà.]
Combines with 就[jiù] for 'as soon as'
No — 刚才 does not form this pattern
Very recent; can loosely cover minutes up to a somewhat longer 'just now' depending on context
Strictly a few minutes ago, within the same conversation/day — never days or weeks (use 最近[zuìjìn] for that)
Can appear with negation 没[méi] on the verb
Yes: 他刚没赶上车。(less common, sounds a bit odd) — usually rephrased
Yes, freely: 刚才没有人来。[Gāngcái méiyǒu rén lái.]

tables.caption_tr: Sentence position patterns
rows: 他刚走。[Tā gāng zǒu.] 'He just left.'
刚[gāng] + Verb + 了[le] + extra info
Subject + 刚 + V + 了 + Time/Object (了 often needed here since a duration/result follows)
他刚来了三天。[Tā gāng lái le sān tiān.] 'He only arrived three days ago.'
刚才我给你打电话了。[Gāngcái wǒ gěi nǐ dǎ diànhuà le.]
我刚才给你打电话了。[Wǒ gāngcái gěi nǐ dǎ diànhuà le.]
刚才[gāngcái] as a standalone answer
你什么时候到的？——刚才。[Nǐ shénme shíhou dào de? — Gāngcái.]
刚才的电话是谁打的？[Gāngcái de diànhuà shì shéi dǎ de?]

tables.caption_tr: Special patterns built with 刚[gāng]
rows: As soon as X happened, Y happened
我刚到家，他就来了。[Wǒ gāng dào jiā, tā jiù lái le.] 'I had only just gotten home when he came.'
我刚好有空。[Wǒ gānghǎo yǒu kòng.] 'I happen to be free.'
A related, more emphatic word — can act like a stronger 刚[gāng] before a verb, and unlike plain 刚 it can sometimes stand alone like 刚才
他刚刚走。[Tā gānggāng zǒu.] 'He just this second left.'

tables.caption_tr: Common mistakes
rows: 刚[gāng] is an adverb and can never stand alone — it always needs a verb right after it. Only 刚才[gāngcái] can be used by itself.
❌ 刚才就到了。 (trying to say 'as soon as arriving')
✅ 我刚到就走了。 [Wǒ gāng dào jiù zǒu le.]
The 刚...就... 'as soon as' pattern uses the adverb 刚[gāng], not the noun 刚才[gāngcái].
❌ 刚才的天气很热。 (meaning 'the weather has been hot recently')
✅ 最近天气很热。 [Zuìjìn tiānqì hěn rè.]
刚才[gāngcái] only covers a few minutes ago, not days or weeks — use 最近[zuìjìn] 'recently' for longer spans.
❌ 他刚才那本书。 (missing a verb)
✅ 他刚才买了那本书。 [Tā gāngcái mǎi le nà běn shū.]
刚才[gāngcái] is a time word, not a verb substitute — the sentence still needs its own verb, just like with 今天[jīntiān] or 现在[xiànzài].

examples.translation_tr: He just left — why are you only arriving now?

daodi-jiujing.title_tr: 到底 / 究竟 ("On Earth, Exactly, After All")
daodi-jiujing.intro_tr: 到底[dàodǐ] and 究竟[jiūjìng] are adverbs that intensify questions, adding a tone of impatience, curiosity, or a demand for a clear, final answer — similar to English "on earth", "exactly", or informally "the hell" (as in "What on earth do you want?"). They must attach to an existing question word (什么, 谁, 哪儿, 怎么, 为什么) or a V-not-V question form — they cannot create a question by themselves and never combine with the particle 吗. 到底 is the everyday spoken choice; 究竟 sounds slightly more formal or literary and is common in writing and serious discussion, but the two are interchangeable in almost all question contexts. Separately, 到底 (only, not 究竟) can also appear in non-question statements meaning "after all, in the end, as one would expect" — a distinct, idiomatic use worth memorizing on its own.

tables.caption_tr: 到底 vs. 究竟: Core Differences
rows: Colloquial, spoken Chinese, very common in daily life
More formal or written; slightly more emphatic/serious in tone
'...on earth...?', '...exactly...?' — demands a clear, final answer
Same meaning; interchangeable with 到底 in almost all question contexts
'in the end', 'after all', 'as one would expect'
Rarely used this way; this idiomatic sense belongs mainly to 到底
Literally 'reach the bottom/end' as a verb complement, e.g. 走到底[zǒu dào dǐ] 'walk to the very end'
Can function as a noun meaning 'the exact situation/outcome', e.g. 弄清究竟[nòngqīng jiūjìng] 'find out the exact truth'
Yes — safe default for speaking; use 到底 in almost any spoken question
Swap in 究竟 when writing essays, news reports, or formal debate questions

tables.caption_tr: Placement of 到底/究竟 in Questions
rows: 你到底想说什么[Nǐ dàodǐ xiǎng shuō shénme]?
What exactly do you want to say?
到底是谁打破了杯子[Dàodǐ shì shéi dǎpòle bēizi]?
Who on earth broke the cup?
你究竟是怎么知道的[Nǐ jiūjìng shì zěnme zhīdào de]?
How on earth did you find out?
你到底去不去[Nǐ dàodǐ qù bu qù]?
Are you going or not — tell me clearly!
他究竟为什么不来[Tā jiūjìng wèishénme bù lái]?
Why on earth isn't he coming?
到底你想怎么样[Dàodǐ nǐ xiǎng zěnme yàng]?
What do you actually want? (extra emphatic, 到底 leads the sentence)

tables.caption_tr: 到底 Meaning 'After All, In the End' (Statements, Not Questions)
rows: 到底 + 是 + [identity/role] justifying a result
他到底是老师[Tā dàodǐ shì lǎoshī]，懂得比我们多。
He is, after all, a teacher — he naturally knows more than we do.
到底 + noun of experience/status ('as expected of...')
到底是老北京[Dàodǐ shì lǎo Běijīng]，什么都知道。
As expected of a native Beijinger, he knows everything.
到底 + 还是 + [the one who really...]
到底还是妈妈了解我[Dàodǐ háishi māma liǎojiě wǒ]。
In the end, it's still mom who understands me best.
footnotes_tr: In this 'after all / as expected' sense only 到底 is used naturally; replacing it with 究竟 sounds odd to native speakers.
This use has no question word and no question mark — it is a statement expressing that a result matches expectations given someone's identity or nature.

tables.caption_tr: Common Mistakes with 到底/究竟
rows: 究竟是老师，懂得多。 (using 究竟 for the 'after all' statement sense)
究竟 does not carry the idiomatic 'as expected, naturally' nuance; it sounds unnatural here
他到底是老师[Tā dàodǐ shì lǎoshī]，懂得比我们多。
你到底想? (dropping the actual question word)
到底/究竟 only intensify an existing question word or V不V form; they cannot form a question alone
你到底想干什么[Nǐ dàodǐ xiǎng gàn shénme]?
你到底累吗? (combining with 吗)
到底/究竟 questions are built with question words or V不V, never with the yes/no particle 吗
你到底累不累[Nǐ dàodǐ lèi bu lèi]?
发生了到底什么事? (placing 到底 after the question word)
到底/究竟 must come before the question phrase they intensify, typically right after the subject
到底发生了什么事[Dàodǐ fāshēngle shénme shì]?

zhihao.title_tr: 只好 (zhǐhǎo): "to have no choice but to, forced to"
zhihao.intro_tr: 只好[zhǐhǎo] means "to have no choice but to..." or "can only...". It introduces the one remaining course of action a speaker is forced to take after other options have been ruled out, usually because of circumstances beyond their control (rain, lack of money, closed shops, illness, etc.). Unlike a free choice, the action after 只好 always carries a tone of reluctance or resignation. It must be followed directly by a verb phrase, never by a bare noun, and the whole sentence is very often preceded by a clause explaining the problem (with 因为, 既然, 没有..., V不到, etc.).

tables.caption_tr: Basic Structure of 只好 [zhǐhǎo]
rows: States the only remaining action, taken reluctantly
Introduces the forced conclusion after explaining the problem
The forced choice is itself a negative action (e.g., not going somewhere)
Marks that the forced action has already happened or become settled

tables.caption_tr: 只好 vs. Similar 'Have No Choice' Expressions
rows: Reluctant last resort after other options fail; followed by the compromise action; neutral/spoken register
他只好道歉。[Tā zhǐhǎo dàoqiàn.] — He had no choice but to apologize.
Stronger sense of compulsion or obligation; more formal, common in writing; often stresses being forced by outside pressure
他不得不道歉。[Tā bùdébù dàoqiàn.] — He was compelled to apologize.
States a limitation or ceiling on ability/options; more neutral, doesn't always imply that alternatives were tried and failed
他只能道歉。[Tā zhǐnéng dàoqiàn.] — All he can do is apologize.
Colloquial combo: first states 'nothing can be done', then names the forced action
没办法,只好道歉了。[Méi bànfǎ, zhǐhǎo dàoqiàn le.] — Nothing to be done, had to apologize.

tables.caption_tr: Common Trigger Clauses That Lead to 只好
rows: Because..., so had no choice but to...
因为下雨,所以只好取消比赛。[Yīnwèi xià yǔ, suǒyǐ zhǐhǎo qǔxiāo bǐsài.] — Because it rained, the match had to be cancelled.
Given that... (a settled fact), then had no choice but to...
既然你不去,我就只好一个人去了。[Jìrán nǐ bú qù, wǒ jiù zhǐhǎo yí ge rén qù le.] — Since you're not going, I'll just have to go alone.
没有(办法/时间/钱)..., 只好...
没有时间做饭,只好叫外卖。[Méiyǒu shíjiān zuò fàn, zhǐhǎo jiào wàimài.] — No time to cook, so had to order delivery.
V bu dào / V bu liǎo..., zhǐhǎo...
Unable to manage V..., so had to...
买不到票,只好改天再去。[Mǎi bu dào piào, zhǐhǎo gǎitiān zài qù.] — Couldn't buy a ticket, so had to go another day.

tables.caption_tr: Key Grammar Rules and Restrictions for 只好
rows: Must be followed by a verb phrase
只好 cannot directly precede a bare noun; it always introduces an action
✓ 只好走路 [zhǐhǎo zǒulù]  ✗ 只好路 (ungrammatical)
只好 implies the choice was forced by circumstance, not a personal preference; use 打算/想 for free plans
打算去 [dǎsuàn qù] (plan to go) — NOT 只好去 unless it's a forced situation
Redundant with 不得不 in the same clause
Both express a forced action in different registers; stacking them is unnatural
✗ 他不得不只好道歉 (redundant, avoid)
Object always comes after the verb
Structure is 只好 + V + (O), never 只好 + O directly
只好吃素菜 [zhǐhǎo chī sùcài] — have no choice but to eat vegetarian dishes
Often closes with 了 for realized situations
了 shows the forced action already took place or the situation is now settled
我只好放弃了。[Wǒ zhǐhǎo fàngqì le.] — I had no choice but to give up.

examples.target: 外面下雨,我们只好在家看电视。
examples.reading: Wàimiàn xià yǔ, wǒmen zhǐhǎo zài jiā kàn diànshì.

examples.target: 商店都关门了,我只好回家。

examples.translation_tr: All the stores were closed, so I had no choice but to go home.

examples.target: 他没有钱买车票,只好走路回家。
examples.reading: Tā méiyǒu qián mǎi chēpiào, zhǐhǎo zǒulù huí jiā.

kongpa.intro_tr: 恐怕[kǒngpà] is an adverb that means "I'm afraid that..." or "probably (something unwelcome)." It is placed before the main verb or before the whole clause to signal that the speaker is making a worried, cautious, or reluctant prediction about something negative, undesirable, or disappointing. Unlike neutral guessing words such as 可能[kěnéng] or 也许[yěxǔ], 恐怕[kǒngpà] always carries a tone of concern, apology, or regret — it is never used for good news. It is extremely common in polite refusals ("I'm afraid I can't..."), cautious estimates ("there are probably as many as..."), and soft warnings ("I'm afraid it's too late"). Because it appears constantly in both spoken and written Chinese, mastering its position and tone is essential for sounding natural and polite.

tables.caption_tr: Basic Sentence Position of 恐怕[kǒngpà]
rows: 我恐怕不能来。[Wǒ kǒngpà bù néng lái.]
恐怕他已经走了。[Kǒngpà tā yǐjīng zǒu le.]
I'm afraid he has already left.
恐怕有一百人。[Kǒngpà yǒu yìbǎi rén.]
There are probably as many as 100 people.
恐怕会下雨。[Kǒngpà huì xià yǔ.]
恐怕来不及了。[Kǒngpà láibují le.]
I'm afraid it's too late now.
footnotes_tr: 恐怕[kǒngpà] must appear before the verb phrase or clause it modifies; it can either follow the subject or open the whole sentence.

tables.caption_tr: 恐怕[kǒngpà] Compared to Other 'Probably/Maybe' Words
rows: worried guess about something negative or unwanted
恐怕来不及了。[Kǒngpà láibují le.] — I'm afraid it's too late.
可能会下雨。[Kěnéng huì xià yǔ.] — It might rain.
也许他忘了。[Yěxǔ tā wàng le.] — Maybe he forgot.
他大概三十岁。[Tā dàgài sānshí suì.] — He's probably around 30.
can't say for sure; result might even be surprising
说不定他会来。[Shuōbudìng tā huì lái.] — He just might come, who knows.
footnotes_tr: Only 恐怕[kǒngpà] inherently implies the speaker hopes the guess is wrong; the others are emotionally neutral.

tables.caption_tr: Common Collocations and Set Phrases with 恐怕[kǒngpà]
rows: 这样恐怕不行。[Zhèyàng kǒngpà bùxíng.]
我恐怕不能参加。[Wǒ kǒngpà bù néng cānjiā.]
恐怕要迟到了。[Kǒngpà yào chídào le.]
I'm afraid we're going to be late.
他恐怕会生气。[Tā kǒngpà huì shēngqì.]
I'm afraid he might get angry.
家里恐怕没有面包了。[Jiāli kǒngpà méiyǒu miànbāo le.]
I'm afraid there's no bread left at home.
就怕你不同意。[Jiù pà nǐ bù tóngyì.]
I'm just afraid you won't agree.
footnotes_tr: 就怕[jiùpà] and 只怕[zhǐpà] are near-synonyms of 恐怕[kǒngpà], often used for extra emphasis in spoken Chinese.

tables.caption_tr: Common Mistakes with 恐怕[kǒngpà]
rows: Placing 恐怕 after the verb: *我不能来恐怕。
恐怕[kǒngpà] must come before the predicate/verb phrase, never after it.
我恐怕不能来。[Wǒ kǒngpà bù néng lái.]
Using 恐怕 for happy or neutral news
恐怕[kǒngpà] always signals worry about something negative; it sounds strange or even sarcastic paired with good news.
可能你考了第一名。[Kěnéng nǐ kǎo le dì-yī míng.] (use 可能, not 恐怕)
Confusing 恐怕 with 害怕[hàipà] ('to fear', a verb)
恐怕[kǒngpà] is an adverb modifying a whole clause; 害怕[hàipà] is a verb meaning 'to be scared of' a specific thing.
我害怕黑暗。[Wǒ hàipà hēi'àn.] vs. 恐怕他不来了。[Kǒngpà tā bù lái le.]
Adding 了[le] at the end often strengthens the 'it has turned out this way' nuance that 恐怕[kǒngpà] implies.
现在出发恐怕来不及了。[Xiànzài chūfā kǒngpà láibují le.]

examples.target: 恐怕明天会下雨。
examples.reading: Kǒngpà míngtiān huì xià yǔ.
examples.translation_tr: I'm afraid it will rain tomorrow.
examples.note_tr: 恐怕[kǒngpà] opens the sentence here, modifying the whole clause that follows.

examples.target: 我恐怕不能参加你的生日聚会。
examples.reading: Wǒ kǒngpà bù néng cānjiā nǐ de shēngrì jùhuì.
examples.translation_tr: I'm afraid I can't attend your birthday party.
examples.note_tr: A polite way to decline an invitation; 恐怕[kǒngpà] softens the refusal.

examples.target: 这个问题恐怕没有那么简单。
examples.reading: Zhège wèntí kǒngpà méiyǒu nàme jiǎndān.

examples.reading: Xiànzài chūfā kǒngpà láibují le.
examples.translation_tr: I'm afraid it's too late to leave now.
examples.note_tr: The final 了[le] adds a 'things have turned out this way' feeling.

examples.target: 他恐怕已经忘了这件事。
examples.reading: Tā kǒngpà yǐjīng wàng le zhè jiàn shì.
examples.translation_tr: I'm afraid he has already forgotten about this matter.

examples.target: 恐怕这次的考试很难。
examples.reading: Kǒngpà zhè cì de kǎoshì hěn nán.
examples.translation_tr: I'm afraid this exam will be very difficult.

examples.reading: Nǐ zhèyàng zuò kǒngpà bú tài héshì.
examples.translation_tr: I'm afraid doing it this way isn't quite appropriate.

qianwan-imperative.title_tr: 千万 (qiānwàn): "Whatever You Do / By All Means" — Urgent Warnings & Exhortations
qianwan-imperative.intro_tr: 千万 [qiānwàn] is an emphatic adverb meaning "whatever you do," "by all means," or "you absolutely must (not)." It is used to deliver urgent warnings or strong exhortations — not to state plain facts. It almost always appears together with 不要/别 ("don't!") or 要 ("must!"), intensifying the imperative force of the sentence. Literally, 千万 means "a thousand ten-thousands" (i.e., an enormous number), and this hyperbole carries over into its grammatical meaning of extreme urgency and emphasis. You'll hear it constantly in spoken warnings between family and friends ("千万别忘了!") and see its more formal cousin 务必 in written notices. Because 千万 cannot stand alone before a bare verb, always pair it with 不要, 别, 要, or 不能.

tables.caption_tr: Core Grammatical Patterns with 千万
rows: Subject + 千万不要 + Verb (+ Object)
Urgent negative warning — the most common pattern
你千万不要迟到。[Nǐ qiānwàn búyào chídào.] "Whatever you do, don't be late."
Same meaning as 千万不要, more colloquial (别 = 不要)
千万别告诉她![Qiānwàn bié gàosu tā!] "Don't tell her, whatever you do!"
千万要小心![Qiānwàn yào xiǎoxīn!] "You must be extremely careful!"
千万 + 不能/不可 + V
Strong prohibition, slightly more formal/serious tone
千万不能放弃。[Qiānwàn bù néng fàngqì.] "You absolutely cannot give up."
used alone as a short reply or added reminder
Emphatic "make sure you do / seriously!" in response to something already said
千万啊!别忘了![Qiānwàn a! Bié wàng le!] "Seriously, don't forget!"

tables.caption_tr: 千万 vs. Similar Emphatic / Modal Words
rows: 不要 / 别 (warning) or 要 (urging)
Strong urgency, spoken, often anxious or caring tone
千万别晚了。[Qiānwàn bié wǎn le.] "Don't be late, whatever you do."
Neutral certainty/emphasis, less urgent than 千万
你一定要来。[Nǐ yídìng yào lái.] "You must definitely come."
请务必准时到场。[Qǐng wùbì zhǔnshí dàochǎng.] "Please be sure to arrive on time."
Neutral — states a rule or requirement, not personal worry
学生必须交作业。[Xuésheng bìxū jiāo zuòyè.] "Students must hand in homework."
Simple, everyday prohibition — no extra urgency implied

tables.caption_tr: Common Fixed Collocations with 千万
rows: pay very close attention, no matter what
no matter what, be careful about safety

tables.caption_tr: Sentence Structure / Word Order
rows: 你, 我们, 大家, etc. — frequently dropped when speaking directly to the listener
Always comes immediately before 不要 / 别 / 要 / 不能 — never after them
不要 / 别 / 要 / 不能
The modal or negation word that 千万 intensifies
The action being warned against or urged
footnotes_tr: 千万 cannot precede a bare verb without 别/不要/要/不能 attached — you cannot say 千万去 to mean 'must go'; the correct form is 千万要去.

tables.caption_tr: Common Mistakes to Avoid
rows: 千万 cannot modify 是 or a plain factual statement — it only intensifies warnings/exhortations
这一定是对的。[Zhè yídìng shì duì de.] (use 一定 instead)
千万 cannot attach directly to a bare verb without a modal marker (要/不要/别/不能)
千万要去做作业。[Qiānwàn yào qù zuò zuòyè.]
千万 cannot combine with 很 + adjective as a plain degree adverb
我一定会很小心。[Wǒ yídìng huì hěn xiǎoxīn.]
Dropping the verb after 不要 leaves the warning incomplete unless the verb is fully clear from context
千万不要忘了。[Qiānwàn búyào wàng le.]

examples.target: 你千万不要告诉他这件事。
examples.reading: Nǐ qiānwàn búyào gàosu tā zhè jiàn shì.
examples.translation_tr: Whatever you do, don't tell him about this.

examples.target: 过马路的时候,千万要小心。
examples.reading: Guò mǎlù de shíhou, qiānwàn yào xiǎoxīn.
examples.translation_tr: When crossing the street, you must absolutely be careful.

examples.target: 千万别迟到,老板会生气的。
examples.reading: Qiānwàn bié chídào, lǎobǎn huì shēngqì de.
examples.translation_tr: Don't be late no matter what — the boss will get angry.

examples.target: 明天考试,你千万不要忘了带铅笔。
examples.reading: Míngtiān kǎoshì, nǐ qiānwàn búyào wàng le dài qiānbǐ.
examples.translation_tr: Tomorrow's the exam — whatever you do, don't forget to bring a pencil.

examples.target: 这个秘密你千万不能说出去。
examples.reading: Zhège mìmì nǐ qiānwàn bù néng shuō chūqu.
examples.translation_tr: You must absolutely not let this secret out.

examples.target: 千万记住,安全第一。
examples.reading: Qiānwàn jìzhu, ānquán dì yī.
examples.translation_tr: Be sure to remember — safety first.

examples.target: 出门在外,千万要照顾好自己。
examples.reading: Chūmén zài wài, qiānwàn yào zhàogù hǎo zìjǐ.
examples.translation_tr: When you're away from home, you absolutely must take good care of yourself.

examples.target: A:我会小心的。 B:千万啊!
examples.reading: A: Wǒ huì xiǎoxīn de. B: Qiānwàn a!
examples.translation_tr: A: I'll be careful. B: You'd better be, no matter what!

shouxian-qici.title_tr: Discourse Sequencers (首先, 其次, 最后)
shouxian-qici.intro_tr: Discourse sequencers like 首先[shǒuxiān] ('first of all'), 其次[qícì] ('secondly'), and 最后[zuìhòu] ('finally') are used to organize spoken or written explanations into a clear, numbered structure — essays, presentations, instructions, or lists of reasons. They are placed at the beginning of each clause or sentence, usually followed by a comma, and each one signals which point in the sequence is being made. This set is more formal than the everyday action-chain words 先[xiān]...然后[ránhòu]...再[zài]..., which describe the order of physical actions rather than abstract points in an argument. Learners often mix the two systems, so this page treats them side by side. Mastering these markers makes it much easier to sound organized and logical in HSK4-level speech and writing."

tables.caption_tr: Core discourse sequencers
rows: Formal/semi-formal; opens the list of points; always clause-initial
Formal; marks the second point; never used without a preceding 首先[shǒuxiān] or 第一[dìyī]
Can mark a third point in a formal list, or mean 'once again' in other contexts
Neutral/casual; links sequential actions or events, not abstract arguments
Narrative continuation; slightly more vivid than 然后[ránhòu]
Closes a list of points or a chain of actions; also works in narratives
第一 / 第二 / 第三
Most formal, numbered-list style; common in written reports, complaints, essays
footnotes_tr: 首先[shǒuxiān], 其次[qícì], and 最后[zuìhòu] belong to the same formal list; mixing them freely with 然后[ránhòu] is common in speech but avoided in formal writing.

tables.caption_tr: Typical sequencing patterns
rows: Formal explanation of reasons, steps, or arguments (essays, speeches)
Mixed register: sequence of actions with a formal opener and closer
Everyday spoken instructions for a series of actions (recipes, directions)
Very formal, numbered enumeration, often in writing
一方面[yì fāngmiàn]...，另一方面[lìng yì fāngmiàn]...
Two parallel aspects of one issue, not necessarily time-ordered
footnotes_tr: The list-opening word (首先[shǒuxiān] / 第一[dìyī] / 一方面[yì fāngmiàn]) sets the register for the whole list — keep the same style through the rest of the sentence.

tables.caption_tr: Formal argument sequence vs. everyday action sequence
rows: Listing reasons or points in an argument
首先[shǒuxiān]...其次[qícì]...最后[zuìhòu]... / 第一[dìyī]...第二[dì'èr]...
Describing a series of physical actions
Presenting two sides of one issue
一方面[yì fāngmiàn]...另一方面[lìng yì fāngmiàn]...
一方面[yì fāngmiàn]...另一方面[lìng yì fāngmiàn]... (used in speech too)
Concluding a narrative about the past
最后[zuìhòu] (as the final event) or 后来[hòulái] (afterwards, later)
footnotes_tr: Do not confuse 最后[zuìhòu] ('finally, as the last item') with 后来[hòulái] ('afterwards, at a later time'); 后来[hòulái] does not close a list, it just moves a story forward in time.

tables.caption_tr: Common mistakes with 首先 / 其次 / 最后
rows: 用 其次[qícì] 但没有 首先[shǒuxiān]
其次[qícì] presupposes an earlier point already introduced by 首先[shǒuxiān] or 第一[dìyī]
Always start the list with 首先[shǒuxiān] or 第一[dìyī] before using 其次[qícì]
把 首先[shǒuxiān] 放在句子中间当动词状语
首先[shǒuxiān] is a discourse marker for a whole clause, not an adverb modifying a single verb
Place 首先[shǒuxiān] at the very start of the clause, followed by a comma
最后[zuìhòu] 与 后来[hòulái] 混用
最后[zuìhòu] closes an enumerated list/final step; 后来[hòulái] simply means 'later on' in a story
Use 最后[zuìhòu] for the last item of a list or process, 后来[hòulái] for 'later' in a narrative
在同一句话里混用两套体系 (e.g. 首先...再...其次...)
Mixing 首先[shǒuxiān]/其次[qícì] with 先[xiān]/再[zài] inconsistently sounds disorganized
Pick one system (formal or casual) and keep it consistent through the whole list

examples.target: 首先，我想说明一下这个计划的目的。
examples.reading: Shǒuxiān, wǒ xiǎng shuōmíng yíxià zhège jìhuà de mùdì.
examples.translation_tr: First of all, I'd like to explain the purpose of this plan.
examples.note_tr: 首先[shǒuxiān] opens a formal list of points; it sits at the very start of the sentence, often followed by a comma.

examples.target: 其次，我们需要考虑成本问题。
examples.reading: Qícì, wǒmen xūyào kǎolǜ chéngběn wèntí.
examples.translation_tr: Secondly, we need to consider the issue of cost.
examples.note_tr: 其次[qícì] introduces the second point in the same list started by 首先[shǒuxiān].

examples.target: 最后，谢谢大家的支持。
examples.reading: Zuìhòu, xièxiè dàjiā de zhīchí.
examples.translation_tr: Finally, thank you everyone for your support.
examples.note_tr: 最后[zuìhòu] closes the list; it can also close a chain of actions, not only abstract points.

examples.target: 首先去超市，然后去图书馆，最后回家。
examples.reading: Shǒuxiān qù chāoshì, ránhòu qù túshūguǎn, zuìhòu huí jiā.
examples.translation_tr: First go to the supermarket, then go to the library, and finally go home.
examples.note_tr: A three-step action chain: 首先[shǒuxiān] → 然后[ránhòu] → 最后[zuìhòu].

examples.target: 学习汉语首先要多听，其次要多说，最后要多写。
examples.reading: Xuéxí Hànyǔ shǒuxiān yào duō tīng, qícì yào duō shuō, zuìhòu yào duō xiě.
examples.translation_tr: To learn Chinese, first you need to listen a lot, secondly speak a lot, and finally write a lot.
examples.note_tr: Here 首先[shǒuxiān] appears mid-sentence after a topic clause, still marking the first sub-point.

examples.target: 第一，价格太贵；第二，质量不好；第三，服务态度差。
examples.reading: Dìyī, jiàgé tài guì; dì'èr, zhìliàng bù hǎo; dìsān, fúwù tàidu chà.
examples.translation_tr: First, the price is too expensive; second, the quality is poor; third, the service attitude is bad.
examples.note_tr: 第一[dìyī]/第二[dì'èr]/第三[dìsān] is the most formal, numbered-list style of sequencing, common in written complaints or reports.

examples.target: 先做作业，再看电视。
examples.reading: Xiān zuò zuòyè, zài kàn diànshì.
examples.translation_tr: Do homework first, then watch TV.
examples.note_tr: 先[xiān]...再[zài]... is the everyday, spoken version for ordering two actions; it is less formal than 首先[shǒuxiān]...其次[qícì]...

examples.target: 我们一方面要提高效率，另一方面也要保证质量。
examples.reading: Wǒmen yì fāngmiàn yào tígāo xiàolǜ, lìng yì fāngmiàn yě yào bǎozhèng zhìliàng.
examples.translation_tr: On the one hand we need to improve efficiency, on the other hand we also need to ensure quality.
examples.note_tr: 一方面[yì fāngmiàn]...另一方面[lìng yì fāngmiàn]... presents two parallel aspects rather than a strict time order.

adjective-reduplication.intro_tr: Many two-syllable (AB) adjectives in Chinese can be reduplicated into an AABB pattern to make the description more vivid, emotionally colorful, and intensified — for example 高兴[gāoxìng] "happy" becomes 高高兴兴[gāogāoxìngxìng] "so happily, cheerfully." This pattern is mostly used in spoken and descriptive language, painting a livelier picture than the plain AB form. Only "quality" adjectives that describe a gradable, subjective state (mood, appearance, condition) can take this pattern — adjectives that classify or relate nouns (like 男[nán] "male" or 主要[zhǔyào] "main") cannot be reduplicated this way. Once reduplicated, the AABB form behaves differently from the plain adjective: it cannot be modified by 很[hěn] or negated with 不[bù], and it usually needs 的[de] (as predicate/attributive) or 地[de] (as adverbial) attached to it. This page gives you the formation rule, tone behavior, grammatical functions, a reference list of common AABB adjectives, and the mistakes to avoid.

tables.caption_tr: Formation Rule: AB → AABB
footnotes_tr: Rule: take the AB adjective, double the first syllable and double the second syllable in order (A+A+B+B), never A+B+A+B.
The reduplication is optional/stylistic — it is not required in normal speech, it adds vividness and emphasis.

tables.caption_tr: Pronunciation & Tone Notes
rows: Unlike single-syllable AA reduplication (e.g. 慢慢[mànman], where the 2nd syllable often becomes neutral tone), in AABB all four syllables normally KEEP their original tone marks.
高高兴兴[gāogāoxìngxìng] — all 4 syllables keep tone 1/1/4/4
In fast, casual speech the very last syllable may be pronounced lightly/shorter, but this is not marked with a written neutral tone in standard textbooks.
漂漂亮亮 pronounced piàopiaoliàngliang colloquially
Don't confuse AABB with the ABB pattern (e.g. 红彤彤[hóngtōngtōng]) — ABB reduplicates only the second syllable and is a different, separate structure used for vivid color/sensory adjectives.

tables.caption_tr: Grammatical Functions of AABB Adjectives
rows: 她穿得漂漂亮亮的[Tā chuān de piàopiaoliàngliàng de]
干干净净的房间[gāngānjìngjìng de fángjiān]
高高兴兴地玩[gāogāoxìngxìng de wán]
收拾得整整齐齐[shōushi de zhěngzhěngqíqí]
多整整齐齐啊![Duō zhěngzhěngqíqí a!]
footnotes_tr: The particle (的 or 地) is almost always required with the AABB form — dropping it sounds incomplete or unnatural in most positions.

tables.caption_tr: Common AABB Adjectives Reference List
Plain AB vs. Reduplicated AABB — Key Differences
rows: No — AABB is not directly negated ✗
Almost always yes, depending on function
Can modify relational adjectives (男, 金, 主要)?
No — only gradable quality adjectives allow AABB

tables.caption_tr: Common Mistakes to Avoid
rows: AABB is already intensified; 很 is redundant/ungrammatical
AABB forms are not directly negated
高兴高兴 (as if repeating the whole word) ✗
This looks like verb reduplication (关心关心), not adjective AABB
主主要要 ✗ / 男男女女... (different meaning) ✗
主要[zhǔyào] is a relational adjective, not a gradable quality adjective
Dropping 的/地 in required positions
她穿得漂漂亮亮 (missing 的) — sounds incomplete
的/地 usually needed to close the AABB phrase grammatically

examples.target: 她[tā]今天[jīntiān]穿[chuān]得[de]漂漂亮亮[piàopiaoliàngliàng]的[de]。
examples.reading: Tā jīntiān chuān de piàopiaoliàngliàng de.
examples.translation_tr: She's dressed very prettily today.

examples.target: 房间[fángjiān]被[bèi]打扫[dǎsǎo]得[de]干干净净[gāngānjìngjìng]。
examples.reading: Fángjiān bèi dǎsǎo de gāngānjìngjìng.

examples.target: 孩子们[háizimen]高高兴兴[gāogāoxìngxìng]地[de]去[qù]公园[gōngyuán]了[le]。
examples.reading: Háizimen gāogāoxìngxìng de qù gōngyuán le.

examples.target: 请[qǐng]老老实实[lǎolǎoshishi]地[de]告诉[gàosu]我[wǒ]实话[shíhuà]。
examples.reading: Qǐng lǎolǎoshishi de gàosu wǒ shíhuà.
examples.translation_tr: Please tell me the truth honestly.

examples.target: 他[tā]把[bǎ]书桌[shūzhuō]收拾[shōushi]得[de]整整齐齐[zhěngzhěngqíqí]。
examples.reading: Tā bǎ shūzhuō shōushi de zhěngzhěngqíqí.
examples.translation_tr: He tidied the desk neatly.

examples.target: 我们[wǒmen]平平安安[píngpíng'ān'ān]地[de]回[huí]家[jiā]了[le]。
examples.reading: Wǒmen píngpíng'ān'ān de huí jiā le.
examples.translation_tr: We returned home safe and sound.

examples.target: 这个[zhège]问题[wèntí]清清楚楚[qīngqīngchǔchǔ]的[de],不用[búyòng]再[zài]解释[jiěshì]了[le]。
examples.reading: Zhège wèntí qīngqīngchǔchǔ de, búyòng zài jiěshì le.
examples.translation_tr: This question is completely clear; there's no need to explain it again.

examples.target: 她[tā]简简单单[jiǎnjiǎndāndān]地[de]回答[huídá]了[le]我[wǒ]的[de]问题[wèntí]。
examples.reading: Tā jiǎnjiǎndāndān de huídá le wǒ de wèntí.

measure-word-reduplication.title_tr: Measure Word Reduplication (个个, 天天: "every")
measure-word-reduplication.intro_tr: Reduplicating a measure word (doubling it, e.g. 个→个个, 天→天天) is a compact way to say "every single one" or "every single (time unit)" in Chinese, similar in meaning to 每 + measure word but more vivid and emphatic. The reduplicated form almost always works together with the adverb 都[dōu] ("all/every") placed right before the verb or adjective, because the doubling itself signals "each one" while 都 confirms "without exception." Only a limited set of common, usually single-syllable measure words reduplicate naturally — 个, 天, 年, 月, 次, 张, 件, 本, 条, 句, 家, and the special word 人 (which is not really a measure word but reduplicates the same way as 人人). Once a measure word is reduplicated, it can no longer carry a number in front of it (you cannot say 三个个); the numeral simply disappears because "every one" already implies totality. This structure typically appears either as the subject of the sentence (referring back to a previously mentioned group) or as a time adverbial expressing habitual/repeated frequency.

tables.caption_tr: Formation Pattern: how measure word reduplication works
rows: 个个都对。[Gègè dōu duì.] "Every single one is correct."

tables.caption_tr: Common measure words that can be reduplicated
rows: every single (long thin thing, e.g. street, rule)

tables.caption_tr: Sentence position: where the reduplicated measure word goes
rows: 个个都很努力。[Gègè dōu hěn nǔlì.] "Every single one works hard."
Stands alone as the subject, referring back to a group already mentioned or implied by context.
天天都下雨。[Tiāntiān dōu xiàyǔ.] "It rains every single day."
Placed before the verb like a frequency adverb; expresses a habitual, repeated action.
这些人,个个都很热情。[Zhèxiē rén, gègè dōu hěn rèqíng.] "These people — every single one of them is warm and friendly."
The noun is stated first as the topic; the reduplicated MW then re-emphasizes "every one of them" without exception.

tables.caption_tr: 每 + Measure Word vs. Reduplicated Measure Word: choosing between them
rows: Neutral; fine in both spoken and written Chinese
More colloquial and vivid; adds emotional emphasis
Often optional; sentence still sounds complete without it
Almost always required; without 都 the sentence sounds incomplete
Range of measure words it works with
Works with virtually any measure word
Only works naturally with a small, fixed set (个, 天, 年, 次, 张, 件, 家, 人...)
Stresses "absolutely every one, with no exception at all"
每个学生都来了。[Měi gè xuésheng dōu lái le.] "Each student came."
学生个个都来了。[Xuésheng gègè dōu lái le.] "The students — every single one came."

tables.caption_tr: Restrictions and common mistakes
rows: The reduplicated measure word almost always needs 都 right after it to complete the sentence
个个都很好。[Gègè dōu hěn hǎo.]
Once a measure word is reduplicated, the totality meaning already replaces any specific number — a numeral cannot stay attached
三本书,本本都很好看。[Sān běn shū, běnběn dōu hěn hǎokàn.]
人 is not a normal measure word
人[rén] reduplicates directly to 人人[rénrén] "everyone" — it does not follow the 一 + MW + 人 pattern of ordinary nouns
人人都爱他。[Rénrén dōu ài tā.]
✗ 人个都爱他。/ ✗ 个人个人都爱他。
Not every measure word reduplicates naturally
Rare or highly specific measure words (e.g. 趟[tàng], 遍[biàn] in some contexts) sound unnatural when doubled; prefer 每 + MW + 都 instead
每趟车都很挤。[Měi tàng chē dōu hěn jǐ.]

examples.target: 个个都很聪明。

fractions-multiples.title_tr: Fractions, Percentages, and Multiples (分之, 倍)
fractions-multiples.intro_tr: Chinese expresses fractions with the pattern denominator + 分之[fēnzhī] + numerator — note this order is the reverse of English ("one third" becomes "three-分之-one"). Percentages are simply a special fraction whose denominator is fixed at 100: 百分之[bǎifēnzhī] + number, e.g. 百分之五十[bǎifēnzhī wǔshí] = 50%. Multiples are expressed with 倍[bèi] ("-fold/times"), used mainly to describe increases and size comparisons (A是B的N倍 = "A is N times B"), but native speakers generally avoid 倍 for decreases — a fraction or percentage is used instead. A key trap is the difference between 增加了N倍[zēngjiā le N bèi] ("increased BY N times," meaning the new total is N+1 times the original) and 增加到N倍[zēngjiā dào N bèi] ("increased TO N times," meaning the new total is exactly N times the original). Mastering these patterns lets you talk about statistics, prices, growth rates, and proportions fluently.

zhi-attributive.title_tr: 之 (zhī): the literary equivalent of 的 (百分之十, 之间)
zhi-attributive.intro_tr: 之 [zhī] is the classical/literary counterpart of the modern possessive-attributive particle 的 [de]. In everyday speech 的 dominates, but 之 survives — and is required — in formal writing, news headlines, legal/academic text, idioms, and especially in a handful of fixed grammatical patterns you cannot replace with 的: fractions/percentages (百分之十 [bǎifēnzhī shí] "ten percent"), the "one of" pattern (之一 [zhī yī]), and location words like 之间 [zhī jiān] "between" or 之后 [zhī hòu] "after". At the HSK5 level, you don't need to produce free literary sentences with 之 — you need to recognize it as "the formal 的" and master the closed set of high-frequency fixed expressions where it appears. Unlike 的, 之 is monosyllabic, cannot take 了/呢 etc. after it, and generally links two elements that are also each fairly short (often single-syllable or classical-flavored words).

yu-preposition.title_tr: 于 (yú): The Literary/Formal Preposition (位于, 等于, 在于)
yu-preposition.intro_tr: 于[yú] is a preposition inherited from Classical Chinese that still survives heavily in modern formal and written Chinese (书面语[shūmiànyǔ]). Unlike 在[zài], 比[bǐ], 给[gěi] or 从[cóng], 于[yú] is almost never used alone in casual speech — it fuses directly onto a preceding verb or adjective to create a single two-syllable formal verb, such as 位于[wèiyú] "to be located at", 等于[děngyú] "to equal", or 在于[zàiyú] "to lie in/consist of". Depending on the verb it attaches to, 于[yú] can silently translate as "in/at", "than", "from", "to/toward", or simply "about", so you must memorize each Verb+于[yú] compound as its own fixed unit rather than translating 于[yú] on its own. Because these compounds sound bookish and precise, they are extremely common in news reports, academic writing, official documents, and essays, but are usually replaced by 在[zài]/比[bǐ]/从[cóng] etc. in everyday conversation. This page collects the core function groups, the most useful fixed compounds, and how they map onto their everyday colloquial equivalents.

tables.caption_tr: Core functions of 于[yú] depending on the verb/adjective it attaches to
column_headers: Meaning of 于 in this pattern
rows: 位于[wèiyú], 在于[zàiyú], 居于[jūyú], 处于[chǔyú]
公司位于市中心。 Gōngsī wèiyú shìzhōngxīn. — The company is located downtown.
等于[děngyú], 高于[gāoyú], 低于[dīyú], 优于[yōuyú], 次于[cìyú], 早于[zǎoyú], 晚于[wǎnyú]
三加二等于五。 Sān jiā èr děngyú wǔ. — Three plus two equals five.
源于[yuányú], 生于[shēngyú], 死于[sǐyú], 毕业于[bìyèyú], 出于[chūyú]
他生于1990年。 Tā shēngyú yī jiǔ jiǔ líng nián. — He was born in 1990.
Object / target of an attitude or action
关于[guānyú], 对于[duìyú], 属于[shǔyú], 忠于[zhōngyú], 致力于[zhìlìyú], 取决于[qǔjuéyú]
这本书属于我。 Zhè běn shū shǔyú wǒ. — This book belongs to me.
善于[shànyú], 敢于[gǎnyú], 勇于[yǒngyú], 易于[yìyú], 难于[nányú]
他善于沟通。 Tā shànyú gōutōng. — He is skilled at communication.

tables.caption_tr: Comprehensive list of common Verb/Adjective + 于[yú] compounds
rows: 学校位于河边。 Xuéxiào wèiyú hébiān. — The school is located by the river.
to equal, to be equivalent to
这等于说他不同意。 Zhè děngyú shuō tā bù tóngyì. — This is equivalent to saying he disagrees.
to lie in, to consist in

to belong to, to fall under
这属于个人隐私。 Zhè shǔyú gèrén yǐnsī. — This falls under personal privacy.
关于这件事,我没有意见。 Guānyú zhè jiàn shì, wǒ méiyǒu yìjiàn. — Concerning this matter, I have no opinion.
对于这个问题,大家看法不同。 Duìyú zhège wèntí, dàjiā kànfǎ bùtóng. — Regarding this issue, everyone's views differ.
由于下雨,活动推迟了。 Yóuyú xiàyǔ, huódòng tuīchí le. — Due to the rain, the event was postponed.
至于价格,我们可以再谈。 Zhìyú jiàgé, wǒmen kěyǐ zài tán. — As for the price, we can discuss it further.
to be good at, skilled in

我们要敢于创新。 Wǒmen yào gǎnyú chuàngxīn. — We must dare to innovate.
他勇于面对失败。 Tā yǒngyú miànduì shībài. — He bravely faces failure.
他忠于自己的信念。 Tā zhōngyú zìjǐ de xìnniàn. — He is loyal to his own beliefs.
本活动限于会员参加。 Běn huódòng xiànyú huìyuán cānjiā. — This event is limited to members.
鉴于情况紧急,我们决定提前出发。 Jiànyú qíngkuàng jǐnjí, wǒmen juédìng tíqián chūfā. — Given the urgency, we decided to leave early.
今年的销量高于去年。 Jīnnián de xiāoliàng gāoyú qùnián. — This year's sales are higher than last year's.
气温低于零度。 Qìwēn dīyú líng dù. — The temperature is below zero.
这个方案优于其他方案。 Zhège fāng'àn yōuyú qítā fāng'àn. — This plan is superior to the other plans.
这个习俗源于古代。 Zhège xísú yuányú gǔdài. — This custom originates from ancient times.

to be devoted to, to strive for

国家正处于发展阶段。 Guójiā zhèng chǔyú fāzhǎn jiēduàn. — The country is currently in a stage of development.
这是基于事实的判断。 Zhè shì jīyú shìshí de pànduàn. — This is a judgment based on facts.

rows: Subject + 位于/在于/处于 + Place/State
Cannot use 于[yú] alone; only the fused compound is grammatical.

Also used figuratively: 'X is tantamount to Y'.

Subject + 的关键/原因/问题 + 在于 + Reason
在于[zàiyú] introduces the key underlying factor, not a physical location.

由于 + Reason, + Result clause (often with 所以[suǒyǐ] or 就[jiù])
