duiyu-guanyu.intro_tr: 对于[duìyú] and 关于[guānyú] both translate roughly as "regarding / about / concerning," and both introduce a noun phrase that the rest of the sentence comments on — but they are not interchangeable. 关于[guānyú] introduces the general *topic* of a discussion, book, article, or report, and the phrase it forms must sit at the very front of the sentence, often ending with 的[de] to modify a following noun. 对于[duìyú] introduces the *target* of an attitude, action, opinion, or evaluation, and it can appear either before or after the subject. Both belong to formal, written-style Chinese (typical of HSK5+ texts, news, essays) and are much less common in casual spoken conversation, where 对[duì] alone is usually preferred.

tables.caption_tr: 对于 vs 关于 at a Glance
rows: "with respect to / toward" — points at the target of an attitude, action, or evaluation
"about / concerning" — introduces the general topic of something
Must come first, before the subject (sentence-initial)
Marks who/what an opinion, feeling, or action is directed at
Marks the subject matter of a book, article, talk, report, or discussion
对于...来说 / 对于...而言 ("as for...")
Very common: 关于...的通知/报告/规定 ("Notice/Report/Regulation about...")
footnotes_tr: In casual speech, both are frequently replaced by the simpler preposition 对[duì].

tables.caption_tr: Sentence Position Patterns
rows: 对于 + Object, Subject + Verb Phrase
对于这件事，我没有意见。 [Duìyú zhè jiàn shì, wǒ méiyǒu yìjiàn.] "Regarding this matter, I have no opinion."
Subject + 对于 + Object + Verb Phrase
我对于这件事没有意见。 [Wǒ duìyú zhè jiàn shì méiyǒu yìjiàn.] "I have no opinion regarding this matter."
关于 + Topic, Subject + Verb Phrase

anzhao-genju.title_tr: 按照 [ànzhào] / 根据 [gēnjù] ("According to, In Accordance With")
anzhao-genju.intro_tr: 按照 [ànzhào] and 根据 [gēnjù] both correspond to English "according to" or "in accordance with," but they carry different nuances. 按照 [ànzhào] is used when an action follows an existing rule, plan, standard, or procedure exactly — think "in compliance with." 根据 [gēnjù] is used when a judgment, conclusion, or decision is based on some source of evidence or information — think "on the basis of." Both words are placed before a noun phrase to form a prepositional phrase that usually precedes the main clause, and both can optionally be followed by 来 [lái] or paired with 进行 [jìnxíng] in more formal writing. Choosing the right one is mostly a matter of whether you are *following* something (按照) or *reasoning from* something (根据).

tables.caption_tr: Core comparison: 按照 [ànzhào] vs 根据 [gēnjù]

basis for reasoning, judgment, or a conclusion

jingguo-tongguo.title_tr: 经过 / 通过 ("via, through, by means of")
jingguo-tongguo.intro_tr: 经过[jīngguò] and 通过[tōngguò] both translate as "through" in English, but they answer different questions. 经过[jīngguò] literally means "to pass through" and is used when something travels through a PLACE, a stretch of TIME, or a PROCESS/EVENT — it describes what you moved through on the way to a result. 通过[tōngguò] literally means "to pass (a test/checkpoint)" and, as a preposition, means "by means of, via" — it introduces the METHOD, CHANNEL, or PERSON that makes a result possible. A simple test: if you can replace it with "after going through..." use 经过[jīngguò]; if you can replace it with "by means of..." use 通过[tōngguò]. Both often appear at the very start of a sentence, before the main subject, forming a background clause that the rest of the sentence comments on.

tables.caption_tr: Core comparison: 经过[jīngguò] vs 通过[tōngguò]
rows: to pass through a place / time / process
Usually at the START of the sentence, before the subject
to pass (a test/vote/checkpoint); by means of
"through, by means of; to pass, be approved"
As a preposition: start of sentence. As a verb: normal verb slot

tables.caption_tr: Sentence patterns and structures
rows: 经过三年的努力,他成功了。 Jīngguò sān nián de nǔlì, tā chénggōng le.
After going through three years of effort, he succeeded.
经过 as main verb (physically pass)
我们经过一条河。 Wǒmen jīngguò yì tiáo hé.
通过[tōngguò] + Method/Person/Channel, + Subject + Verb (+ 达到[dádào]/得到[dédào]/使[shǐ] + Result)
通过学习,他提高了水平。 Tōngguò xuéxí, tā tígāole shuǐpíng.
Through studying, he raised his level.
他通过了考试。 Tā tōngguòle kǎoshì.
Negation of 通过 (fail / not approved)
他没通过考试。 Tā méi tōngguò kǎoshì.
He did not pass the exam.

tables.caption_tr: 经过[jīngguò]: three typical uses
rows: 他经过我家门口。 Tā jīngguò wǒ jiā ménkǒu.
He passes by the front of my house.
经过一个月的治疗,他好了。 Jīngguò yí gè yuè de zhìliáo, tā hǎo le.
After a month of treatment, he recovered.
经过调查,警察找到了真相。 Jīngguò diàochá, jǐngchá zhǎodàole zhēnxiàng.
After (going through) the investigation, the police found the truth.

tables.caption_tr: 通过[tōngguò]: two typical uses
rows: 通过这个软件,我们可以聊天。 Tōngguò zhège ruǎnjiàn, wǒmen kěyǐ liáotiān.
By means of this app, we can chat.
2. To PASS/be APPROVED (exam, law, proposal, inspection)
这项法律已经通过了。 Zhè xiàng fǎlǜ yǐjīng tōngguò le.
This law has already been passed.

tables.caption_tr: Common confusable words
column_headers: Key difference from 经过/通过
rows: Focuses on what was traversed, not the tool used to get the result
Focuses on the method/channel, or on succeeding a test/approval
to pass by (a place), usually in passing/incidentally
Only for PLACE, more casual, often implies "just happened to pass", no process/means meaning
through (a physical medium, e.g. glass, window); also "through/via" in some formal writing (Taiwan usage close to 通过)
透过[tòuguò] is more literal/physical (light through glass) or regional formal equivalent of 通过[tōngguò]

tables.caption_tr: Quick decision guide
rows: Did something move across a place, a period of time, or an event?
Is this the method/tool/person that makes the result possible?
通过努力... (by means of effort...)
Did someone pass an exam, a bill, or an inspection?
Is it just casually passing a location, with no emphasis on process?
footnotes_tr: Both 经过[jīngguò] and 通过[tōngguò], when used as prepositions, typically open the sentence as a background clause, and the main subject + comment follows afterward.
通过[tōngguò] as a preposition is often paired with result verbs like 达到[dádào] (to reach/achieve), 得到[dédào] (to obtain), 使[shǐ] (to make/cause) later in the sentence.
经过[jīngguò] cannot mean "pass an exam"; only 通过[tōngguò] (or colloquially 过[guò]) is used for that meaning.

yiji.intro_tr: 以及[yǐjí] is a formal written-style conjunction meaning "and, as well as, together with." It typically appears just before the final item in a list, linking it to everything mentioned before, and it often signals that the last item is somewhat secondary or additional in importance compared to the earlier ones. Unlike 和[hé], which mainly joins nouns, 以及[yǐjí] can connect noun phrases, verb phrases, and even short clauses, making it common in reports, news articles, official documents, and academic writing. It is rarely used in casual spoken conversation, where 和[hé] or 跟[gēn] are preferred instead. Because it belongs to 书面语[shūmiànyǔ] (written register), using it correctly is a strong marker of formal, educated writing style.

tables.caption_tr: Core Function of 以及 [yǐjí]
rows: Formal, written style (书面语[shūmiànyǔ]); not used in casual speech
Placed right before the last item in a list of two or more items
Nouns / noun phrases, verb phrases, and even short clauses
The item(s) after 以及[yǐjí] are often felt to be additional or slightly less central than the item(s) before it
Cannot join two single subjects that are the sole subject of a sentence the way 和[hé] often does in short spoken sentences (e.g. avoid 我以及你 in casual speech)

tables.caption_tr: Sentence Patterns with 以及 [yǐjí]

经济发展以及环境保护 [jīngjì fāzhǎn yǐjí huánjìng bǎohù]
Two noun phrases (topics) linked as related but separate concerns.
提高效率以及降低成本 [tígāo xiàolǜ yǐjí jiàngdī chéngběn]
以及 + 其他/所有 + N
以及其他相关问题 [yǐjí qítā xiāngguān wèntí]
"as well as other related issues" — a very common closing phrase in reports.
这项政策以及与它相关的措施 [zhè xiàng zhèngcè yǐjí yǔ tā xiāngguān de cuòshī]

tables.caption_tr: 以及 [yǐjí] vs Similar Conjunctions
rows: Before the last (often secondary) item in a list
历史、现状以及未来 [lìshǐ, xiànzhuàng yǐjí wèilái] — "history, current state, and future"
Between two items, or before the last item in a short list
我和你 [wǒ hé nǐ] — "you and I"
Between two items in written text
理论与实践 [lǐlùn yǔ shíjiàn] — "theory and practice"
Between two items in daily speech
我跟他 [wǒ gēn tā] — "he and I"
Very formal / written, often legal or official
Between items in lists, especially official ones
本人及家属 [běnrén jí jiāshǔ] — "the person and their family members"

tables.caption_tr: Common Collocations with 以及 [yǐjí]
Common Mistakes with 以及 [yǐjí]
rows: 我以及我朋友去看电影。
我和朋友去看电影。[Wǒ hé péngyou qù kàn diànyǐng.]
以及[yǐjí] is too formal for casual, everyday statements about people doing things together; use 和[hé] or 跟[gēn] instead.
苹果以及香蕉都很好吃。 (in casual shopping talk)
苹果和香蕉都很好吃。[Píngguǒ hé xiāngjiāo dōu hěn hǎochī.]
For simple, everyday lists of two items, 和[hé] sounds natural; 以及[yǐjí] sounds stiff/overly formal here.
以及 used to join only two short single-syllable nouns
Reserve 以及[yǐjí] for lists of 2+ items, especially the final item in a longer or more formal list
以及[yǐjí] works best with fuller phrases or longer lists, not the shortest, most casual pairs.
Placing 以及 between every item in a list (A以及B以及C)
A、B以及C — commas between earlier items, 以及 only before the last
以及[yǐjí] normally appears only once, right before the final item, not repeated between every pair.

zhiyu.title_tr: 至于 (zhìyú): "As For..., When It Comes To..."
zhiyu.intro_tr: 至于[zhìyú] means "as for," "as to," or "when it comes to." It is used to shift the conversation from a topic that has already been mentioned to a new, separate topic — often one that is less important, less certain, or simply different from what came before. 至于[zhìyú] always starts its own clause: it is followed directly by a noun, a question word, or a whole clause, and then a comment about that new topic follows. Because it signals a *shift* away from the previous point, it is rarely the very first thing said in a conversation — there is usually something mentioned right before it. Don't confuse it with 对于[duìyú] "regarding" or 关于[guānyú] "about," which introduce the topic of an opinion or discussion without implying any shift.

tables.caption_tr: Basic Sentence Pattern with 至于[zhìyú]
rows: Introduces a brand-new topic to comment on
至于[zhìyú]钱,你别担心。 (As for the money, don't worry.)
Shifts from what was just discussed to a related but separate topic
我下午有空,至于[zhìyú]晚上,我还不确定。
至于 + Topic + 嘛/呢, + Comment
Softens the topic shift, adds a conversational pause
至于[zhìyú]结果嘛,现在还不好说。
zhìyú + 是否/为什么/能不能..., ...
Introduces an unresolved sub-question as the new topic
至于[zhìyú]他能不能来,还得看情况。

tables.caption_tr: 至于[zhìyú] vs Similar Topic-Introducing Words
rows: as for / when it comes to (shifts to a new, separate topic)
Marks that the speaker is now leaving the previous topic and moving to a different one
我会去,至于[zhìyú]他去不去,我不管。
Introduces the object of an opinion, attitude, or action; no topic shift implied
对于[duìyú]这个问题,我有不同的看法。
Introduces the general subject matter of a talk, book, or discussion
关于[guānyú]中国历史,他知道得很多。
Casual/spoken; often triggers a related thought, not necessarily a shift away
说到[shuōdào]吃的,我最喜欢火锅。
Formal/written; evaluates something from one specific angle
就[jiù]价格而言[éryán],这家比较便宜。

tables.caption_tr: Common Collocations and Extended Patterns
rows: 至于[zhìyú]价钱嘛,我们可以商量。
zhìyú...jiù gèng bú yòng shuō le
as for..., that goes without saying
至于[zhìyú]他的中文水平,就更不用说了。
even, to the extent that (stronger version of 甚至)
他忙得甚至于[shènzhìyú]没时间吃饭。
not go so far as to... (a related but separate grammar point)
他不至于[búzhìyú]连这个都不懂吧。
to such an extent that... (introduces a resulting, often negative, outcome)
他太累了,以至于[yǐzhìyú]睡着了。

tables.caption_tr: Common Mistakes with 至于[zhìyú]
rows: 至于 cannot open a sentence out of nowhere as a plain topic marker; it needs a prior topic to shift away from
我很喜欢中国菜。 (至于[zhìyú] is unnecessary here)
*用至于表达'关于这份报告'的意思
That meaning ('about/concerning') belongs to 关于[guānyú], not 至于[zhìyú]
关于[guānyú]这份报告,我有几点意见。
*把至于放在分句中间当介词用
至于 must begin its own clause/topic — it cannot sit mid-clause like a normal preposition
..., 至于[zhìyú]其他问题,我们以后再说。
*把至于和不至于当成同一个词
至于[zhìyú] = 'as for' (topic marker); 不至于[búzhìyú] = 'not go so far as to' (a different structure and meaning)
See the separate 不至于[búzhìyú] topic for details

examples.target: 至于这个问题,我们以后再讨论。
examples.reading: Zhìyú zhège wèntí, wǒmen yǐhòu zài tǎolùn.
examples.translation_tr: As for this question, we'll discuss it later.
examples.note_tr: 至于[zhìyú] opens a new topic (this question) that is being set aside for now.

examples.target: 我喜欢吃中国菜,至于日本菜,我没吃过。
examples.reading: Wǒ xǐhuan chī Zhōngguó cài, zhìyú Rìběn cài, wǒ méi chīguo.
examples.translation_tr: I like Chinese food; as for Japanese food, I've never had it.
examples.note_tr: Shows the classic pattern: Topic 1 discussed, then 至于[zhìyú] shifts to Topic 2.

examples.target: 他会不会来,我不知道,至于时间,他也没说。
examples.reading: Tā huì bu huì lái, wǒ bù zhīdào, zhìyú shíjiān, tā yě méi shuō.
examples.translation_tr: I don't know whether he'll come; as for the time, he didn't mention that either.
examples.note_tr: 至于[zhìyú] introduces yet another separate unresolved sub-topic (the time).

examples.target: 至于钱的问题,你不用担心。
examples.reading: Zhìyú qián de wèntí, nǐ búyòng dānxīn.
examples.translation_tr: As for the money issue, you don't need to worry.

examples.target: 你想去就去吧,至于我嘛,还是留在家里比较好。
examples.reading: Nǐ xiǎng qù jiù qù ba, zhìyú wǒ ma, háishi liú zài jiā lǐ bǐjiào hǎo.
examples.translation_tr: If you want to go, go ahead; as for me, I'd rather stay home.
examples.note_tr: 至于...嘛 softens the topic shift in casual speech.

examples.target: 这次考试大家都及格了,至于成绩好不好,那是另外一回事。
examples.reading: Zhè cì kǎoshì dàjiā dōu jígé le, zhìyú chéngjì hǎo bu hǎo, nà shì lìngwài yì huí shì.
examples.translation_tr: Everyone passed this exam; as for whether the grades are good, that's another matter.

examples.target: 至于他为什么不来,我们也搞不清楚。
examples.reading: Zhìyú tā wèishénme bù lái, wǒmen yě gǎo bu qīngchu.
examples.translation_tr: As for why he didn't come, we're not clear on that either.
examples.note_tr: 至于[zhìyú] can introduce a whole question clause (为什么...) as the new topic.

zhi-suoyi.title_tr: 之所以...是因为... ('The reason ... is because ...')
zhi-suoyi.intro_tr: 之所以[zhīsuǒyǐ]...是因为[shì yīnwèi]... is a formal, written-style structure that flips the normal cause→result order: instead of stating the reason first, it puts the RESULT (the surprising or notable fact) first, and then explains WHY. Literally, 之所以 means roughly "the reason that [this is so]" (之 is a literary linking particle, and 所以 here is not the everyday "so/therefore" but literally "that by which"), followed by 是因为 "is because." This pattern is common in essays, news reports, and explanations where the writer wants to draw attention to a result before justifying it. It always appears in a single sentence with a Subject/Topic + 之所以 + [Result Clause] + ，是因为 + [Reason Clause] shape, and cannot be mixed with 因为 at the start of the same clause.

tables.caption_tr: Core structure and word order
rows: The person, thing, or event being explained (他, 这个计划, 公司...)
Fixed marker introducing the RESULT clause; comes right after the subject, never before it
States the fact, outcome, or behavior that needs explaining
Comma + 'is because' — introduces the REASON clause
States the actual cause; may end with 的 for extra emphasis: ...是因为...的

tables.caption_tr: 之所以...是因为... vs. 因为...所以... — order and emphasis
rows: 因为下雨，所以我没去。[yīnwèi xiàyǔ, suǒyǐ wǒ méi qù.] 'Because it rained, I didn't go.'
Highlights the result first, then justifies it
我之所以没去，是因为下雨。[wǒ zhī suǒyǐ méi qù, shì yīnwèi xiàyǔ.] 'The reason I didn't go is because it rained.'

tables.caption_tr: Common variants of the reason clause
rows: 'is mainly because' — signals there may be other minor reasons too
Adds 的 at the very end for stronger, more conclusive emphasis (common in speech-like formal explanations)

tables.caption_tr: 之所以 as part of a noun phrase (之所以...的原因/是...)
rows: S + 之所以 + V(O) + 的原因
Turns the whole clause into a noun phrase meaning 'the reason that S does X' — often followed by 是, 就是, or used after 知道/了解
之所以 + V(O) + 是有原因的
'There is a reason why...' — softer, introductory framing before giving the actual reason

tables.caption_tr: Common mistakes
rows: 之所以 cannot follow 因为; the two overlap in function and cannot co-occur at the start
他之所以是因为堵车迟到。
是因为 clause must come AFTER the full result clause, not be inserted in the middle
他之所以迟到，是因为堵车。
Using 所以 again in the reason clause is redundant; the reason clause needs 是因为, not 所以
Placing 之所以 before the subject
之所以 must follow the subject/topic if one is stated
他之所以... (not 之所以他...)

examples.target: 他之所以迟到，是因为堵车了。
examples.reading: tā zhī suǒyǐ chídào, shì yīnwèi dǔchē le.
examples.translation_tr: The reason he was late is because there was a traffic jam.

examples.target: 我之所以学习汉语，是因为我对中国文化很感兴趣。
examples.reading: wǒ zhī suǒyǐ xuéxí Hànyǔ, shì yīnwèi wǒ duì Zhōngguó wénhuà hěn gǎn xìngqù.
examples.translation_tr: The reason I study Chinese is because I'm very interested in Chinese culture.

examples.target: 这个计划之所以失败，是因为准备不足。
examples.reading: zhège jìhuà zhī suǒyǐ shībài, shì yīnwèi zhǔnbèi bùzú.
examples.translation_tr: The reason this plan failed is because the preparation was insufficient.

examples.target: 她之所以能成功，是因为她一直很努力。
examples.reading: tā zhī suǒyǐ néng chénggōng, shì yīnwèi tā yìzhí hěn nǔlì.
examples.translation_tr: The reason she was able to succeed is because she has always worked hard.

examples.target: 之所以取消比赛，是因为天气不好。
examples.reading: zhī suǒyǐ qǔxiāo bǐsài, shì yīnwèi tiānqì bù hǎo.
examples.translation_tr: The reason the match was cancelled is because the weather was bad.

examples.target: 我之所以没告诉你，是因为不想让你担心。
examples.reading: wǒ zhī suǒyǐ méi gàosu nǐ, shì yīnwèi bù xiǎng ràng nǐ dānxīn.
examples.translation_tr: The reason I didn't tell you is because I didn't want to make you worry.

examples.target: 公司之所以决定裁员，主要是因为经济不景气。
examples.reading: gōngsī zhī suǒyǐ juédìng cáiyuán, zhǔyào shì yīnwèi jīngjì bù jǐngqì.
examples.translation_tr: The reason the company decided to lay off staff is mainly because of the poor economy.

examples.target: 你知道他之所以这么做的原因吗？
examples.reading: nǐ zhīdào tā zhī suǒyǐ zhème zuò de yuányīn ma?
examples.translation_tr: Do you know the reason why he acted this way?

er-contrast.intro_tr: 而[ér] is a formal, written-register (书面语[shūmiànyǔ]) conjunction that links two words, phrases, or clauses of the same grammatical type — most often two adjectives, two verbs, or two verb phrases. Its exact meaning ('and' vs 'but') is decided entirely by the logical relationship between the two halves: if they are compatible or reinforcing, 而 means 'and/while'; if they clash, 而 means 'but/yet'. It also appears in the fixed patterns 因...而...[yīn...ér...] ('because of...') and 为...而...[wèi...ér...] ('for the sake of...'), where it links a cause/purpose to an action, and it can attach a manner adverbial to a verb much like 地[de]. Because it belongs to formal written Chinese, 而 is common in essays, news, speeches, and classical-flavored idioms, but is rarely used in casual spoken conversation (where 但是, 可是, 和, or simply juxtaposition are preferred). Mastering 而 mainly means learning to read the semantic relationship between the two elements it joins, plus memorizing its handful of fixed collocational patterns.

tables.caption_tr: The Two Core Meanings of 而 — Decided by Logical Relationship
rows: A and B are compatible / reinforce each other
A and B are opposite / clash
B happens right after A / as a consequence of A
to stand out (lit. break through the sheath and emerge)
而 attaches a manner word to the verb that follows
而 marks a shift from one stage/state to another
from...to..., in the course of becoming...
由弱而强[yóu ruò ér qiáng]

tables.caption_tr: Fixed Structural Patterns Built on 而
rows: introduces a cause (formal equivalent of 因为...所以...)
He was absent due to illness.
introduces a purpose (formal equivalent of 为了)
由 + Starting point + 而 + Endpoint
yóu qiǎn ér shēn de jiǎngjiě
explain, going from shallow to deep
He was just joking, that's all.
时 + A + 而 + 时 + B
Tiānqì shí lěng ér shí rè.
The weather is now cold, now hot.
一 + V + 再 + 而 + V

tables.caption_tr: Common Four-Character Idioms Built with 而 (memorize as fixed units)
rows: so imposing it inspires fear at first sight
reap without sowing; get something for nothing
to stand out, to distinguish oneself
to let something pass with a mere smile
to go downstream / to go with the flow

tables.caption_tr: 而 vs. Other 'and / but' Words: When to Use Which
rows: adjectives, verbs, verb phrases, clauses (parallel structure required)

tables.caption_tr: Grammatical Requirements and Common Mistakes
rows: A and B must be grammatically parallel
而 needs two elements of the same type (Adj+Adj, V+V, VP+VP) — it cannot join a noun to a verb
*简单而实用性 (Adj + Noun — breaks parallelism)
而 is not used to list plain nouns
For simple noun lists use 和/以及/跟, not 而
而 rarely starts a spoken sentence casually
在口语[kǒuyǔ] (casual speech) prefer 但是/可是/不过 instead of a bare sentence-initial 而
而，我觉得不行。 (sounds unnatural in casual speech)
而已[éryǐ] always goes at the very end of the sentence
It closes the sentence, meaning 'that's all' — cannot appear mid-sentence
因...而... needs a nominalized or short cause, not a full independent clause
The 因 clause should read like a reason phrase, not a complete separate sentence
*因他没有钱了而辍学 (awkward, too long/independent)

examples.target: 他学习努力而认真。
examples.reading: Tā xuéxí nǔlì ér rènzhēn.
examples.translation_tr: He studies hard and conscientiously. (additive 而: joins two positive qualities)

examples.target: 这个方法简单而有效。
examples.reading: Zhège fāngfǎ jiǎndān ér yǒuxiào.
examples.translation_tr: This method is simple yet effective. (additive/mild-contrast 而: two compatible qualities)

examples.target: 华而不实的话不可信。
examples.reading: Huá ér bù shí de huà bù kě xìn.
examples.translation_tr: Flashy-but-empty words cannot be trusted. (contrastive 而, fixed four-character idiom 华而不实[huá'ér bùshí])

examples.target: 他因病而缺席了会议。
examples.reading: Tā yīn bìng ér quēxí le huìyì.
examples.translation_tr: He was absent from the meeting due to illness. (因...而... cause pattern)

examples.target: 大家都在为共同的目标而努力。
examples.reading: Dàjiā dōu zài wèi gòngtóng de mùbiāo ér nǔlì.
examples.translation_tr: Everyone is working hard for a common goal. (为...而... purpose pattern)

examples.target: 岁月匆匆而过。
examples.reading: Suìyuè cōngcōng ér guò.
examples.translation_tr: The years passed by in a hurry. (而 links a manner adverb to the following verb, like 地)

examples.target: 学而时习之，不亦说乎？
examples.reading: Xué ér shí xí zhī, bú yì yuè hū?
examples.translation_tr: To learn and, from time to time, practice what one has learned — is this not a joy? (classical sequential 而, from the Analects)

examples.target: 他由小职员而成为公司总裁。
examples.reading: Tā yóu xiǎo zhíyuán ér chéngwéi gōngsī zǒngcái.
examples.translation_tr: He went from being a lowly clerk to becoming the company's president. (而 marks a transition/progression between two stages)

conger.title_tr: 从而 [cóng'ér]: "thus, thereby, and as a result"
conger.intro_tr: 从而 [cóng'ér] is a formal, written-style conjunction meaning "thus," "thereby," or "and as a result." It links two clauses in a single sentence, where the second clause describes a result, achievement, or further action that becomes possible BECAUSE OF the action, method, or situation stated in the first clause. Unlike a simple cause-effect word such as 所以 [suǒyǐ], 从而 [cóng'ér] carries the sense of "through this means, this outcome was accomplished," so the two clauses usually share the same subject (the subject of clause 2 is typically omitted). You will mainly meet 从而 [cóng'ér] in essays, news reports, academic writing, and formal speeches — it sounds too stiff for casual conversation. It is often paired with 通过 [tōngguò] ("through/by means of") or 由于 [yóuyú] ("due to") in the first clause to set up the means before stating the result.

tables.caption_tr: Core Structure of 从而 [cóng'ér]
rows: States what is done, or the means/condition
Often introduced by 通过 [tōngguò] or 由于 [yóuyú], but can also stand alone
= 'thus, thereby'; formal written register only, never sentence-initial on its own
States the outcome made possible by clause 1
Subject is normally the same as clause 1 and is usually omitted
footnotes_tr: Pattern: Subject + Predicate1 (means/reason), 从而 + Predicate2 (result achieved through Predicate1).

tables.caption_tr: 从而 [cóng'ér] vs Similar Result Connectors
rows: 'thereby' — result achieved THROUGH the means in clause 1
Formal writing, news, can start a new sentence
'thus, hence' — similar to 从而 but weaker means-to-end sense
footnotes_tr: 因此 [yīncǐ] and 所以 [suǒyǐ] can begin a brand-new sentence; 从而 [cóng'ér] normally cannot — it must join two clauses within one sentence.

tables.caption_tr: Common Collocations and Patterns with 从而 [cóng'ér]
rows: 通过[tōngguò]改革[gǎigé]，从而[cóng'ér]提高[tígāo]了[le]效率[xiàolǜ]。 — 'Through reform, [we] thereby raised efficiency.'
由于[yóuyú]技术[jìshù]进步[jìnbù]，从而[cóng'ér]降低[jiàngdī]了[le]成本[chéngběn]。 — 'Because of technological progress, costs were thereby lowered.'
他[tā]提出了[tíchūle]新[xīn]方案[fāng'àn]，从而[cóng'ér]解决了[jiějuéle]问题[wèntí]。 — 'He proposed a new plan, thereby solving the problem.'
改革[gǎigé]从而[cóng'ér]使[shǐ]经济[jīngjì]更加[gèngjiā]繁荣[fánróng]。 — 'The reform thereby made the economy more prosperous.'
footnotes_tr: 使 [shǐ] after 从而 [cóng'ér] introduces a causative result and lets the second clause take a new object without breaking the same-subject tendency of 从而.

tables.caption_tr: Common Mistakes with 从而 [cóng'ér]
rows: ✗ 他努力工作，从而他的老板很满意。
他努力工作，从而得到了[dédàole]老板[lǎobǎn]的[de]认可[rènkě]。 — 'He worked hard, thereby earning his boss's recognition.'
Clause 2's subject should match clause 1's; if the subject truly changes, use 因此 [yīncǐ] instead
我[wǒ]饿[è]了[le]，所以[suǒyǐ]去[qù]吃饭[chīfàn]了[le]。 — 'I was hungry, so I went to eat.'
从而 [cóng'ér] is written/formal register; use 所以 [suǒyǐ] in everyday speech
Starting a new sentence with 从而
...从而[cóng'ér]提高[tígāo]了[le]效率[xiàolǜ]。 (kept within one sentence)
Unlike 因此 [yīncǐ], 从而 [cóng'ér] cannot stand as a sentence-initial connector for a new sentence
Using it for a simple negative/unwanted consequence
他[tā]生病[shēngbìng]了[le]，所以[suǒyǐ]没[méi]来[lái]上课[shàngkè]。 — 'He got sick, so he didn't come to class.'
从而 [cóng'ér] implies clause 2 is an achievement/outcome enabled by clause 1's action, not just any resulting fact

examples.target: 政府加大了教育投入，从而提高了教学质量。
examples.reading: Zhèngfǔ jiādàle jiàoyù tóurù, cóng'ér tígāole jiàoxué zhìliàng.
examples.translation_tr: The government increased investment in education, thereby raising the quality of teaching.

examples.target: 他努力学习，从而考上了理想的大学。
examples.reading: Tā nǔlì xuéxí, cóng'ér kǎoshàngle lǐxiǎng de dàxué.
examples.translation_tr: He studied hard, and thereby got into his dream university.

examples.target: 公司引进了新技术，从而大大降低了生产成本。
examples.reading: Gōngsī yǐnjìnle xīn jìshù, cóng'ér dàdà jiàngdīle shēngchǎn chéngběn.
examples.translation_tr: The company introduced new technology, thereby greatly reducing production costs.

examples.target: 通过长期锻炼，他的身体变得更健康，从而提高了工作效率。
examples.reading: Tōngguò chángqī duànliàn, tā de shēntǐ biàn de gèng jiànkāng, cóng'ér tígāole gōngzuò xiàolǜ.
examples.translation_tr: Through long-term exercise, his health improved, and thus his work efficiency increased.

examples.target: 这项政策减少了污染，从而改善了城市的空气质量。
examples.reading: Zhè xiàng zhèngcè jiǎnshǎole wūrǎn, cóng'ér gǎishànle chéngshì de kōngqì zhìliàng.
examples.translation_tr: This policy reduced pollution, thereby improving the city's air quality.

examples.target: 科学家发现了新的证据，从而证明了这个理论。
examples.reading: Kēxuéjiā fāxiànle xīn de zhèngjù, cóng'ér zhèngmíngle zhège lǐlùn.
examples.translation_tr: Scientists discovered new evidence, thereby proving this theory.

examples.target: 我们必须改进生产流程，从而使产品质量得到保证。
examples.reading: Wǒmen bìxū gǎijìn shēngchǎn liúchéng, cóng'ér shǐ chǎnpǐn zhìliàng dédào bǎozhèng.
examples.translation_tr: We must improve the production process, thereby ensuring that product quality is guaranteed.

faner.intro_tr: 反而[fǎn'ér] is an adverb meaning "on the contrary" or "instead," used to introduce a result that is the opposite of what logic or the preceding context would lead you to expect. It always sits after the subject of its own clause and directly before the verb phrase — it can never open a sentence with no subject in front of it. It is very frequently paired with 不但不/没(有)[búdàn bù/méi(yǒu)] to build a strong "not only not X, but on the contrary Y" reversal. Compared with 却[què], which marks a mild, neutral turn, 反而 carries a stronger sense of surprise, irony, or defiance of expectation — it says "this is the opposite of what should have happened."

tables.caption_tr: Core Structure & Position of 反而[fǎn'ér]
rows: 他反而更喜欢了。[Tā fǎn'ér gèng xǐhuan le.]
反而 always sits after the subject and before the verb phrase.
我说了半天，反而没用。[Wǒ shuōle bàntiān, fǎn'ér méiyòng.]
Subject dropped in clause 2 because it's the same as clause 1's subject.
Subject + 不但不/没(有) + VP1，反而 + VP2
他不但没生气，反而笑了。[Tā búdàn méi shēngqì, fǎn'ér xiào le.]
Strongest, most common contrast pattern — intensifies the reversal.
反而 cannot precede its own subject; it must come AFTER the subject, and there must be a preceding clause setting up the expectation.

tables.caption_tr: 反而 vs. Similar Contrast Words (却 / 反倒 / 相反)
rows: Contrary to expectation/logic — "instead, on the contrary"
天气不但没变暖，反而更冷了。[Tiānqì búdàn méi biàn nuǎn, fǎn'ér gèng lěng le.]
Strongest sense of a reversed, unexpected outcome; needs an implied expectation.
A mild turn or contrast — "but, yet"
他很努力，却没考上。[Tā hěn nǔlì, què méi kǎoshàng.]
Weaker and more neutral than 反而; extremely common in both speech and writing.
你帮他，他反倒骂你。[Nǐ bāng tā, tā fǎndào mà nǐ.]
More spoken/casual; interchangeable with 反而 in most everyday contexts.
"On the contrary" — often opens a new sentence
他没生气，相反，他笑了。[Tā méi shēngqì, xiāngfǎn, tā xiào le.]
Formal/written; can stand alone at the start of a sentence followed by a comma, unlike 反而.

tables.caption_tr: Common Fixed Patterns Using 反而
rows: Not only not X, but on the contrary Y
他不但不道歉，反而说是我的错。[Tā búdàn bú dàoqiàn, fǎn'ér shuō shì wǒ de cuò.]
他越解释，我反而越糊涂。[Tā yuè jiěshì, wǒ fǎn'ér yuè hútu.]
这个方法不仅没有帮忙，反而添乱。[Zhège fāngfǎ bùjǐn méiyǒu bāngmáng, fǎn'ér tiānluàn.]
X, 反而 Y (Y is the surprising outcome)
吃了药，他反而更难受了。[Chīle yào, tā fǎn'ér gèng nánshòu le.]

tables.caption_tr: Common Mistakes with 反而
rows: 反而 is placed before the subject, which is not allowed.
他反而生气了。[Tā fǎn'ér shēngqì le.]
Using 反而 for a plain, neutral difference
反而 requires an implied expectation being broken, not just any contrast.
Use 但是[dànshì] or 却[què] instead for a plain, neutral contrast.
反而 cannot be fronted with a comma the way 相反 can.
相反，他还在工作。[Xiāngfǎn, tā hái zài gōngzuò.] or 他反而还在工作。[Tā fǎn'ér hái zài gōngzuò.]
反而 needs a preceding clause establishing what was expected, otherwise the sentence sounds incomplete.
Always state the expected situation first, then follow with 反而 + the surprising result.

fouze-buran.title_tr: 否则 / 不然 ("otherwise, or else")
fouze-buran.intro_tr: 否则[fǒuzé] and 不然[bùrán] both translate as "otherwise" or "or else" in English. They link two clauses: the first states an action, suggestion, requirement, or fact, and the second (introduced by 否则/不然) states the unwanted result that will happen if the first clause is NOT followed. Think of it as "Do X, otherwise (if you don't) Y will happen." 否则 is more formal and common in writing, while 不然 is the everyday spoken choice; both words are interchangeable in most contexts. They are almost always placed at the very start of the second clause, and the second clause frequently ends with 就 + verb or 会...的 to mark the predicted consequence.

tables.caption_tr: Basic Sentence Formula
rows: A statement, suggestion, command, or fact
Often contains 要, 得, 应该, or is a plain imperative
你要多喝水[Nǐ yào duō hē shuǐ] (You need to drink more water)
否则[fǒuzé] / 不然[bùrán] (+ optional 的话[de huà])
Means "otherwise, or else"; placed at the start of Clause B
The undesired result if Clause A is not followed
Often uses 就[jiù], 会...的[huì...de], or 不会[bú huì]
否则你会生病的[fǒuzé nǐ huì shēngbìng de] (otherwise you'll get sick)

tables.caption_tr: 否则 vs 不然: Key Differences
rows: Formal, common in writing, news, essays
Possible but rare (否则的话[fǒuzé de huà])
Very common (不然的话[bùrán de huà])
No — 要否则 is not used
Yes — 要不然[yàobùrán] is very common
Can be used alone as a reply
Yes — "不然呢?[Bùrán ne?]" = "What else (would it be)?"

tables.caption_tr: The 否则/不然 Word Family
rows: otherwise / also used to mean "how about..."

tables.caption_tr: Common Patterns Inside Clause B (the Consequence)
rows: 否则就迟到了[fǒuzé jiù chídào le]
不然会感冒的[bùrán huì gǎnmào de]
否则/不然 + 不会...[bú huì]
否则他不会生气[fǒuzé tā bú huì shēngqì]
otherwise he wouldn't be angry (used to justify an inference about a fact already known)
否则/不然 + 别想...[bié xiǎng]
不然你别想及格[bùrán nǐ bié xiǎng jígé]
otherwise you can forget about passing

tables.caption_tr: Common Mistakes
rows: 否则/不然 used with no Clause A stated
否则/不然 needs a preceding condition or action to contrast against — it cannot open a conversation
Add Clause A first: 你得努力，否则会失败[Nǐ děi nǔlì, fǒuzé huì shībài]
要 cannot combine directly with 否则
Use 要不然[yàobùrán] instead of 要否则
Using 否则 in very casual daily chat
Sounds overly formal/stiff for small everyday requests
Use 不然[bùrán] or 要不[yàobù] in casual speech
不然的话不然 (repeating the connector)
Redundant — the concessive meaning is only needed once
Pick one form: either 不然 alone, or 不然的话, not both together
Placing 否则/不然 mid-clause B instead of at its start
否则/不然 must open Clause B, not appear after the subject
Say 否则你会迟到[fǒuzé nǐ huì chídào], not 你否则会迟到

hekuang.title_tr: 更/何况 (hékuàng): 'Let Alone, Not to Mention'
hekuang.intro_tr: 何况[hékuàng] is a rhetorical connective meaning "let alone," "not to mention," or "much less." It links two clauses where the first states an already-extreme or easily-accepted case, and 何况[hékuàng] introduces a second case that is even MORE obviously true, making a rhetorical point rather than asking a real question — no answer is expected. It very often pairs with 连[lián]...都/也[dōu/yě]... in the first clause to set up the extreme example. Adding 更[gèng] before it (更何况[gèng hékuàng]) intensifies the emphasis, roughly "moreover, and even more so..." 何况[hékuàng] belongs to fairly formal/written register but is also common in spoken argumentative speech.

tables.caption_tr: Core structure of 何况[hékuàng]
rows: Clause A (extreme/easy case), 何况[hékuàng] + Clause B (?)
A is already true/hard, let alone B — B is even more obviously true
他跑不过我，何况[hékuàng]你？ (I can already outrun him, let alone you?)
连[lián] + extreme case + 都/也[dōu/yě] + V，何况[hékuàng] + comparison case
Sets up an extreme baseline, then says the second case is even more so
连[lián]小孩都[dōu]懂，何况[hékuàng]大人。 (Even a child understands, let alone an adult.)
Adds extra emphasis: 'moreover, and even more so...'
更何况[gèng hékuàng]现在没时间了。 (Moreover, there's no time now.)
Softer rhetorical question tag, common in speech
他都不去，何况[hékuàng]我呢? (He's not even going, let alone me?)

tables.caption_tr: 何况[hékuàng] vs. similar connectives
rows: Links a stronger, obvious-conclusion clause after a first example
Same as 何况 but stronger emphasis
Often used to add a decisive final reason in an argument
'Moreover, besides' — adds an extra supporting reason
Does NOT need a preceding extreme example like 何况 does; simply adds a new point
'Not to mention...', very colloquial equivalent of 何况
Interchangeable with 何况 in most everyday contexts
'Let alone... even more so...' — combines 别说 with 何况 for double emphasis
别说[biéshuō]小孩，连大人也不懂，更何况[gèng hékuàng]老人。

tables.caption_tr: Typical sentence-building patterns
rows: 连[lián] + Subject + 都/也[dōu/yě] + Verb Phrase (negative or hard fact)
Even X can't/won't do it — how could Y possibly?
X is already true, and even more so is Y
On top of that, there's also the fact that... (adds weight to an argument)
Not even A, let alone B (a noun, not a full clause)

tables.caption_tr: Common fixed collocations
rows: Used when the second item in the comparison is a noun phrase rather than a full clause
Adds that there is an ADDITIONAL factor making the situation even more extreme
The most common intensified form; almost fixed as one emphatic connector
Adds a soft rhetorical-question tone; very natural in spoken argument

youyu-daozhi.title_tr: 由于 / 导致 ('Due to... / To lead to...')
youyu-daozhi.intro_tr: 由于[yóuyú] and 导致[dǎozhì] are two formal, written-style words used to express cause and effect, common in news reports, essays, and official speech (HSK5 level). 由于[yóuyú] is a conjunction/preposition that introduces the CAUSE of something — it is a more formal substitute for 因为[yīnwèi] and, unlike 因为[yīnwèi], can attach directly to a noun phrase without a full clause. 导致[dǎozhì] is a verb meaning "to lead to / to result in / to cause," and it almost always introduces a NEGATIVE or undesirable outcome — it sits between the cause and the bad result, functioning as the main verb of the sentence. The two words are frequently combined in the pattern 由于...，导致... to give a complete, formal cause-and-effect sentence. This page also compares 由于[yóuyú]/导致[dǎozhì] with their near-synonyms 因为[yīnwèi], 造成[zàochéng], 引起[yǐnqǐ], and 使[shǐ] so you can choose the right word for the right register and connotation.

tables.caption_tr: Core vocabulary: word class, meaning, and register
rows: because of, due to, owing to
to lead to, to result in, to cause
to give rise to, to trigger

tables.caption_tr: Sentence patterns with 由于[yóuyú]
rows: 由于[yóuyú] + Cause，所以[suǒyǐ]/因此[yīncǐ]/因而[yīn'ér] + Result
由于[yóuyú] introduces the cause; a connector like 所以[suǒyǐ] can optionally head the result clause, but is often omitted
The comma alone can link cause and result; no connector needed — common in written style
由于[yóuyú] can follow the subject instead of opening the sentence: 他[tā] 由于[yóuyú] 生病[shēngbìng]，没[méi] 来[lái] 上课[shàngkè]
Unlike 因为[yīnwèi], 由于[yóuyú] readily takes a bare noun phrase: 由于[yóuyú] 天气[tiānqì] 原因[yuányīn]
The most common formal cause-effect pattern at HSK5 level

tables.caption_tr: Sentence patterns with 导致[dǎozhì]
rows: 交通[jiāotōng] 堵塞[dǔsè] 导致[dǎozhì] 迟到[chídào] — the traffic jam caused lateness
marks the causing as already realized/completed
Result + 是[shì] 由于[yóuyú] + Cause + 导致的[dǎozhìde]
puts emphasis on the cause: 事故[shìgù] 是[shì] 由于[yóuyú] 疏忽[shūhu] 导致的[dǎozhìde]
导致[dǎozhì] + Result 的[de] 原因[yuányīn] 是[shì] + Cause
reverses order to foreground the cause as the answer
footnotes_tr: 导致[dǎozhì] is a transitive verb: it must be followed directly by the resulting event/state, never by 所以[suǒyǐ] or another connector.

tables.caption_tr: 由于[yóuyú] vs 因为[yīnwèi]: formal vs neutral cause markers
rows: neutral, used in speech and writing
Can attach directly to a noun phrase
yes — 由于[yóuyú] 天气[tiānqì] 原因[yuányīn]
less natural alone; usually needs a clause or 因为...的关系[de guānxi]
Pairs with 所以[suǒyǐ] in result clause
yes, common and often expected in spoken Chinese
yes, less common in this position
Can be used alone to answer 'why?'
yes — 因为[yīnwèi] 我[wǒ] 很[hěn] 忙[máng]

tables.caption_tr: 导致[dǎozhì] vs near-synonyms: 造成[zàochéng], 引起[yǐnqǐ], 使[shǐ]
rows: a serious/abstract negative outcome (failure, accident, decline)
导致[dǎozhì] 失败[shībài] — lead to failure
造成[zàochéng] 损失[sǔnshī] — cause a loss
引起[yǐnqǐ] 注意[zhùyì] — draw attention
any adjective or verb phrase result, general causative
neutral, can be positive or negative
使[shǐ] 人[rén] 高兴[gāoxìng] — make people happy
footnotes_tr: 导致[dǎozhì] and 造成[zàochéng] are almost never used for positive outcomes; for positive results use 使[shǐ] or 带来[dàilái] ('bring about') instead.

examples.reading: Yóuyú xiàyǔ, bǐsài qǔxiāo le.

suizhe.intro_tr: 随着[suízhe] is a formal connector meaning "along with, as, in step with" — it introduces a changing situation (usually growth, development, or passage of time), and the main clause that follows describes a parallel, correlated change. Think of it as "As X changes, Y also changes accordingly." It almost always sits at the very beginning of the sentence, is followed by a noun phrase describing a process (often ending in 发展/提高/变化/增长/推移 etc.), and is separated from the main clause by a comma. It is common in news reports, essays, and formal speech, and the second clause frequently contains words like 也[yě], 越来越[yuèláiyuè], 逐渐[zhújiàn], or 不断[búduàn] to reinforce the sense of ongoing, correlated change. Unlike 因为...所以... (which expresses strict cause-and-effect), 随着 simply links two things that develop together over time.

tables.caption_tr: Basic Structure of 随着[suízhe]
rows: 随着[suízhe] + Noun Phrase describing a change/process
The phrase after 随着 must express an ongoing process, not a static fact
Always separates the 随着-clause from the main clause
Subject + (也/越来越/逐渐/不断) + Predicate
Describes the result/change that happens in parallel

tables.caption_tr: Common Collocations: 随着[suízhe] + ... + 的[de] + ...
随着[suízhe] vs Similar Words
rows: Formal, sentence-initial; introduces a changing condition that another clause changes along with
Most common in written/formal Chinese; needs two correlated changes
Concrete, often physical following, not abstract cause-effect
伴随着[bànsuízhe]音乐[yīnyuè]声[shēng]，他们[tāmen]跳[tiào]起[qǐ]舞[wǔ]来[lái]。
Stronger literary flavor, common in essays
'At the same time' — links two simultaneous events
经济[jīngjì]发展[fāzhǎn]了[le]，与此同时[yǔcǐtóngshí]环境[huánjìng]问题[wèntí]也[yě]出现[chūxiàn]了[le]。
Simultaneity only, not a correlated-change relationship
Bound morpheme used in compounds (随时/随后/随手), cannot open a sentence alone like 随着
Not a full connective by itself

tables.caption_tr: Adverbs Commonly Used in the Second Clause
rows: 'gradually, little by little' (slightly less formal than 逐渐)

tables.caption_tr: Common Mistakes with 随着[suízhe]
rows: Confusing 随着 with 因为 (strict cause-effect)
随着 links two things that change together over time; it is not a logical 'because' reason
✗ 随着[suízhe]我[wǒ]很[hěn]忙[máng]，我[wǒ]没[méi]去[qù]。 → ✓ 因为[yīnwèi]我[wǒ]很[hěn]忙[máng]，所以[suǒyǐ]我[wǒ]没[méi]去[qù]。
Using 随着 with a static noun (no process implied)
The phrase after 随着 must describe change/development (发展/提高/变化/增长/推移...), not a fixed fact
✗ 随着[suízhe]他[tā]是[shì]老师[lǎoshī]... → ✓ 随着[suízhe]他[tā]年龄[niánlíng]的[de]增长[zēngzhǎng]...
Leaving out the parallel change in the main clause
The second clause should show a corresponding change (often with 也/越来越/逐渐/不断), otherwise the sentence feels unfinished
✗ 随着[suízhe]经济[jīngjì]的[de]发展[fāzhǎn]，中国[Zhōngguó]。 → ✓ 随着[suízhe]经济[jīngjì]的[de]发展[fāzhǎn]，中国[Zhōngguó]越来越[yuèláiyuè]强大[qiángdà]了[le]。
Forgetting the comma between the two clauses
随着-clause and the main clause must be visually/prosodically separated
✗ 随着经济的发展人们变富了 (run together) → ✓ 随着[suízhe]经济[jīngjì]的[de]发展[fāzhǎn]，人们[rénmen]变[biàn]富[fù]了[le]

yilai.intro_tr: 以来 [yǐlái] attaches to a time expression to mean "since [that time point], continuously up until now." It always looks backward from the present and implies that a state, situation, or repeated action has gone on without a break during that whole span. 以来 is very often paired with 自 [zì] or 自从 [zìcóng] at the front of the time phrase to form 自...以来 or 自从...以来, though a bare Time Word + 以来 is also completely correct on its own. Unlike 以后 [yǐhòu], which just marks "after a point" with no promise that anything continues to the present, 以来 specifically stresses the entire uninterrupted stretch from then until now — and for that reason it can never be used to talk about the future.

tables.caption_tr: Basic Structure Patterns
rows: 今年以来[jīnnián yǐlái],他一直在学习汉语。
Bare time word directly before 以来; very common in speech and writing.
自去年以来[zì qùnián yǐlái],物价一直在上涨。
自 adds a slightly more formal, written-style 'from'.
自从 + [Time Point or Clause] + 以来, ...
自从他离开以来[zìcóng tā líkāi yǐlái],我们没有再见过面。
自从 can introduce a full event or clause, not just a bare time noun, making it more flexible than 自.

tables.caption_tr: Common Fixed Collocations with 以来
rows: for a long time (up until now)
长期以来,这个问题一直没有解决。[Chángqī yǐlái, zhège wèntí yìzhí méiyǒu jiějué.]
这是有史以来最大的一次地震。[Zhè shì yǒushǐ yǐlái zuìdà de yí cì dìzhèn.]
多年以来,他一直住在北京。[Duōnián yǐlái, tā yìzhí zhù zài Běijīng.]
一直以来,她都很努力。[Yìzhí yǐlái, tā dōu hěn nǔlì.]
since the founding of the country
建国以来,中国发生了巨大的变化。[Jiànguó yǐlái, Zhōngguó fāshēngle jùdà de biànhuà.]
入夏以来,天气一直很热。[Rùxià yǐlái, tiānqì yìzhí hěn rè.]

tables.caption_tr: 以来 vs. 以后 vs. 自从 — How They Differ
column_headers: Can a bare Time Word attach directly?
rows: 'since X, continuously until now' — continuity is required
三年以来[sān nián yǐlái],他每天锻炼。 (has exercised every day for 3 years, still ongoing)
'after X' — no promise that anything continues
any point after X: past, present, or future
下课以后[xiàkè yǐhòu],我们去吃饭。 (a single, one-time future action)
'ever since X (an event or moment)' — usually needs 以来/就/都 later in the sentence
No — normally needs an event/clause, and pairs with 以来/就/都/一直
自从搬家以来[zìcóng bānjiā yǐlái],他就很少运动。

tables.caption_tr: Grammar Constraints and Common Mistakes
rows: 以来 only points from past to present, never to the future
从明天开始[cóng míngtiān kāishǐ],我要努力学习。
✗ 明天以来,我要努力学习。
以来 cannot be attached to a future time word; use 从...开始 or 从...起 instead for future plans.
The clause after 以来 needs ongoing/repeated meaning, not one isolated event
这个月以来,他一直很忙。[Zhège yuè yǐlái, tā yìzhí hěn máng.]
✗ 这个月以来,他去了一次上海。
以来 signals a continuous state or repeated action across the whole span, not a single completed trip.
Word order is fixed: Time Phrase + 以来
以来 always comes AFTER the time expression it modifies, never before it.
The main clause often (though not always) adds 一直/都/常常 to reinforce continuity
自从她结婚以来,一直住在上海。
△ 自从她结婚以来,住在上海。 (sounds incomplete/unnatural)
Continuity adverbs like 一直, 都, 常常 make the 'unbroken since then' meaning explicit and are strongly preferred in natural speech and writing.

tables.caption_tr: Typical Position of the 以来-Phrase in a Sentence
rows: 这几年以来[zhè jǐ nián yǐlái],他变化很大。 (As for these past few years, he has changed a lot.)
他这几年以来[tā zhè jǐ nián yǐlái]变化很大。 (He, over these past few years, has changed a lot.)

ningke-yebu.title_tr: 宁可...也不... ("I would rather... than...")
ningke-yebu.intro_tr: 宁可...也不... [nìngkě...yě bù...] is a preference structure meaning "would rather (do A) than (do B)" — it expresses that between two undesirable or costly options, the speaker chooses the lesser evil (A), and firmly rejects the other option (B), even if A itself is unpleasant or difficult. Unlike 与其...不如..., which is a neutral comparison of two options where the second is simply "better," 宁可...也不... carries a strong, often stubborn or determined emotional tone — the speaker is willing to accept a real sacrifice or hardship rather than do the second thing. It is HSK5-level written/spoken formal register, common in arguments, principled statements, and moral stances. The second clause almost always contains a negative (不 or 不愿意/不肯) referring to the rejected action.

tables.caption_tr: Core structure of 宁可...也不...
rows: States what the speaker is willing to accept, even if unpleasant
States what the speaker refuses to do, no matter what
也不愿意 [yě bú yuànyì] / 也不肯 [yě bù kěn]
Adds emphasis: 'is not even willing to...'
Subject + 宁可 + A，(subject) + 也不 + B
Subject can appear once before 宁可 and be omitted in the second clause, or repeated

tables.caption_tr: Common variants and synonyms
rows: Emphasizes personal wish/willingness ('would rather, prefer to')
Similar to 宁可, slightly more colloquial, emphasizes willingness to endure
Shortened literary form, found in set phrases like 宁死不屈 [nìng sǐ bù qū] 'would rather die than yield'
Same logic but second clause is positive: 'would rather A in order to achieve/do B'

tables.caption_tr: 宁可...也不... vs 与其...不如...
rows: Would rather A than B (reject B)
Rather than B, it's better to do A
B (rejected option) comes first, A (better option) comes second
Strong, resolute, sometimes stubborn or sacrificial
Neutral, rational comparison of two choices
Often something difficult or costly that speaker accepts
我宁可累一点儿，也不愿意麻烦别人。
与其麻烦别人，不如自己做。 [Yǔqí máfan biérén, bùrú zìjǐ zuò.]

tables.caption_tr: Common collocations in Clause B (rejection)
rows: refuses to, will not consent to...

tables.caption_tr: Common errors to avoid
rows: 宁可累一点儿，不愿意麻烦别人 (missing 也)
也 is required before 不 in Clause B; it links back to 宁可 and adds 'even'
宁可累一点儿，也不愿意麻烦别人
与其累一点儿，也不麻烦别人 (mixing patterns)
与其 pairs with 不如, not with 也不
与其麻烦别人，不如自己做 OR 宁可累一点儿，也不麻烦别人
Using 宁可...也不... for neutral preferences without hardship
This pattern implies willingness to endure something costly in A; for simple preference use 更喜欢 or 与其...不如...
Use 我更喜欢... for plain preference without sacrifice

yaome-yaome.intro_tr: 要么[yàome]...要么[yàome]... is a paired conjunction meaning "either...or..." It presents two (or more) mutually exclusive options, and the listener/speaker must pick exactly one — the other option(s) are excluded. This structure is used only in statements, never to form a "or" question (that job belongs to 还是[háishi]). Each alternative gets its own 要么[yàome], and the two halves are grammatically parallel, working equally well with single words, verb phrases, or full clauses with their own subjects. A very common idiomatic extension is 要么[yàome]不X，要么[yàome]就[jiù]Y, which expresses an "all-or-nothing" attitude — either skip X entirely, or commit fully to Y.

tables.caption_tr: Basic Structure: 要么[yàome] A, 要么[yàome] B
rows: introduces the second, mutually exclusive alternative
A 要么[yàome] B 要么[yàome]
'either A or B' — exactly one must be chosen, not both, not neither
footnotes_tr: 要么[yàome] historically combines 要[yào] ('to want / will') with the light suffix 么[me]; it is closely related to 要不[yàobù] and 要不然[yàoburán] ('otherwise').
Both 要么[yàome] clauses should be structurally parallel (same type of phrase repeated) for the sentence to sound natural.

tables.caption_tr: Formation with Different Grammatical Units
rows: Either go to Beijing, or go to Shanghai.
要么[yàome]咖啡[kāfēi]，要么[yàome]茶[chá]，你[nǐ]选[xuǎn]一个[yí ge]吧[ba]。
Either coffee or tea — pick one.
Either you come, or I'll go.
要么[yàome]看[kàn]电影[diànyǐng]，要么[yàome]逛[guàng]街[jiē]，要么[yàome]在[zài]家[jiā]休息[xiūxi]。
Either watch a movie, go shopping, or rest at home.

tables.caption_tr: 要么[yàome] vs 或者[huòzhě] vs 还是[háishi]: Choosing the Right 'Or'
rows: presents mutually exclusive choices; strongly implies a decisive either/or
要么[yàome]吃[chī]饭[fàn]，要么[yàome]睡觉[shuìjiào]。 'Either eat or sleep.'
simply lists alternatives, no strong exclusivity emphasis; can also mean 'or perhaps'
你[nǐ]可以[kěyǐ]写[xiě]信[xìn]或者[huòzhě]打[dǎ]电话[diànhuà]。 'You can write a letter or call.'
used in 'A 还是 B?' alternative questions to ask which option the listener wants
你[nǐ]要[yào]咖啡[kāfēi]还是[háishi]茶[chá]？ 'Do you want coffee or tea?'
footnotes_tr: A frequent beginner mistake is using 还是[háishi] inside a statement where 要么[yàome] or 或者[huòzhě] is needed — 还是[háishi] is reserved for questions.

tables.caption_tr: Special Idiomatic Patterns with 要么[yàome]
rows: 要么[yàome]不 X，要么[yàome]就[jiù] Y
'either not X at all, or Y (properly)' — an all-or-nothing attitude
要么[yàome]不[bù]做[zuò]，要么[yàome]就[jiù]做[zuò]好[hǎo]。 'Either don't do it, or do it well.'
lists three exclusive options in a row
要么[yàome]坐[zuò]火车[huǒchē]，要么[yàome]坐[zuò]飞机[fēijī]，要么[yàome]开[kāi]车[chē]去[qù]。 'Either take the train, fly, or drive there.'
要么[yàome] X，要么[yàome] Y，反正[fǎnzhèng]...
combines with 反正[fǎnzhèng] ('anyway, in any case') to show the outcome doesn't matter much
要么[yàome]今天[jīntiān]，要么[yàome]明天[míngtiān]，反正[fǎnzhèng]这[zhè]星期[xīngqī]得[děi]完成[wánchéng]。 'Either today or tomorrow — anyway it must be finished this week.'

tables.caption_tr: Common Mistakes
rows: Do not mix 要么[yàome] with 还是[háishi] in the same construction — both halves need 要么[yàome], and 还是[háishi] belongs to questions, not this statement pattern.
要么[yàome]...要么[yàome]... is a declarative structure; it cannot be turned into a 吗[ma]-question.
Don't combine 要么[yàome] and 或者[huòzhě] together in the same pair — choose one conjunction system for the whole sentence.
*要么不去，要么去了也没关系。
In the 要么不X要么就Y pattern, the second clause normally takes 就[jiù] to reinforce the decisive/committed tone.

examples.target: 要么你去，要么我去，两个人不用都去。

bushi-jiushi.title_tr: 不是[búshì]...就是[jiùshì]... ('If Not X, Then Y' / 'Either...Or...')
bushi-jiushi.intro_tr: 不是[búshì]...就是[jiùshì]... literally means "if it isn't X, then it is Y," and is used to state that of two known possibilities, one of them is always the case — nothing else happens. Unlike 要么[yàome]...要么[yàome]..., which offers a future choice between two options, 不是[búshì]...就是[jiùshì]... describes an existing pattern or recurring reality, and very often carries a complaining, exasperated, or resigned tone ("it's always one thing or the other!"). Both slots (A and B) must be the same grammatical type — two verb phrases, two nouns, or two adjectives — and the whole structure usually needs a time word (每天[měitiān], 最近[zuìjìn], 周末[zhōumò]) or a habitual context to make sense. This pattern is extremely common in spoken Chinese for describing habits, complaints, and recurring situations.

tables.caption_tr: Core structure of 不是[búshì]...就是[jiùshì]...
rows: (主语) + 不是 + A，就是 + B
Of two known possibilities, it is always A or B
States a recurring fact, not a hypothetical choice
每天/常常/最近 + 不是...就是...
Adds a time/frequency word to frame the habitual pattern
Very common combination; the time word signals repetition
A and B must match grammatically
Both slots must be the same type: V/VP, N, or Adj
不是[V]就是[V], 不是[N]就是[N], 不是[Adj]就是[Adj]
不是 A，就是 B，反正/总之 C
búshì A, jiùshì B, fǎnzhèng/zǒngzhī C
footnotes_tr: 不是[búshì] here does NOT negate a following clause the way plain 不是[búshì] does elsewhere — the whole pair functions as one fixed linking pattern.

tables.caption_tr: 不是[búshì]...就是[jiùshì]... vs. similar 'either...or...' patterns
rows: either A or B (stating an existing fact)
Describes reality/habit; often has a complaining tone; no real choice involved
Offers a genuine choice between future options, neutral tone
More formal/written; can link options in statements without implying complaint
Corrects a wrong assumption; A and B are NOT both true — only B is
Expresses uncertainty about which is true, not an exhaustive real pattern
footnotes_tr: Confusing 不是...就是... with 不是...而是... is a very common beginner error — they look alike but mean opposite things.

tables.caption_tr: Typical content in the two slots (what native speakers actually put there)
rows: 不是加班就是开会 [búshì jiābān jiùshì kāihuì]
不是感冒就是发烧 [búshì gǎnmào jiùshì fāshāo]
不是在家就是在公司 [búshì zài jiā jiùshì zài gōngsī]
不是你的错就是我的错 [búshì nǐ de cuò jiùshì wǒ de cuò]
不是太快就是太小声 [búshì tài kuài jiùshì tài xiǎoshēng]

tables.caption_tr: Common mistakes
rows: 你不是就是要去，要去就快点。
你不是要去就是不去，快决定。
The two slots must contain a real either/or content, not a repeated fragment; also mind word order after 不是[búshì]/就是[jiùshì]
他不是学生就是老师喜欢运动。 (unclear which noun the extra clause belongs to)
他不是学生，就是老师，反正他喜欢运动。
Keep the sentence structured with a clear final comment clause (反正[fǎnzhèng]/总之[zǒngzhī]) separate from the two alternatives
我今天不是在公司，而是在家。 / 我不是在公司，就是在家。
Don't mix 不是...而是... (correction) with 不是...就是... (alternation) — pick one pattern
Using 不是...就是... for a future choice you are offering someone: 你不是喝茶就是喝咖啡吧？(sounds odd)
你要喝茶还是喝咖啡？ / 你可以要么喝茶要么喝咖啡。
Use 还是[háishi] or 要么[yàome]...要么[yàome]... when actually offering a choice, not 不是...就是...

bushi-ershi.intro_tr: 不是[búshì]...而是[érshì]... is a paired structure meaning "not A, but rather B," used to explicitly reject one idea and replace it with the correct one. It goes beyond simple negation (不 alone) because it always supplies the corrected alternative in the same breath, making it a favorite tool for clarifying misunderstandings, correcting assumptions, or sharpening contrasts in both speech and writing. The two halves can frame nouns, verb phrases, adjectives, or entire reason clauses, and the structure works in subject position, predicate position, or as an embedded explanation (e.g. "it's not that..., but that..."). Note the tone sandhi: 不 before the 4th-tone 是 is pronounced bú. This pattern is distinct from 不是...就是... (either A or B, expressing uncertainty) and from 不但...而且... (not only A but also B, which adds rather than rejects).

tables.caption_tr: Core Structure of 不是...而是...
rows: 不是[búshì]中国人[Zhōngguórén] — "not a Chinese person"
Asserts B as the actual truth
而是[érshì]日本人[Rìběnrén] — "but rather a Japanese person"
S + 不是[búshì] A，而是[érshì] B。
"S is not A, but rather B"

tables.caption_tr: What Can Fill Slot A and Slot B
rows: Most common use — identifying people or things
Very common pattern: correcting a misunderstood reason ('it's not that..., but that...')

tables.caption_tr: 不是...而是... vs. Similar Paired Patterns
rows: States that one fact is wrong and gives the correct fact
Speaker is unsure which of two options is true — not a correction
not only A but also B (addition)
Adds a second true fact; does not reject the first one
States two facts side by side without the connective 而[ér], milder emphasis

tables.caption_tr: Common Mistakes with 不是...而是...
rows: Using bare 而[ér] instead of 而是[érshì] before a noun
而[ér] alone usually links verbs/adjectives, not bare nouns
Use 而是[érshì] + noun: 不是[búshì]苹果[píngguǒ]，而是[érshì]香蕉[xiāngjiāo]。
Dropping 不是[búshì] and using only 而是[érshì]
而是[érshì] cannot stand alone; it needs the negated first half for the contrast to make sense
Always pair both halves: 不是[búshì] A，而是[érshì] B
而是[érshì] expresses certainty about the correct alternative; 就是[jiùshì] expresses uncertainty between two guesses
Choose based on meaning: correction (而是[érshì]) vs. guessing (就是[jiùshì])
Reversing the order, putting B before A
The rejected idea (A) must always come first, followed by the true one (B)
Keep strict order: 不是[búshì] A，而是[érshì] B — never reverse

tables.caption_tr: 不是...而是... in Different Sentence Roles
rows: 这[zhè]不是[búshì]我的[wǒ de]错[cuò]，而是[érshì]你的[nǐ de]错[cuò]。
This isn't my fault, but rather yours.
Reason clause ('it's not that..., but that...')
我[wǒ]不[bù]去[qù]不是[búshì]因为[yīnwèi]懒[lǎn]，而是[érshì]因为[yīnwèi]生病[shēngbìng]了[le]。
I'm not going not because I'm lazy, but because I got sick.
他[tā]不是[búshì]慢慢[mànmàn]走[zǒu]的[de]，而是[érshì]跑[pǎo]着[zhe]走[zǒu]的[de]。
He didn't walk slowly — he ran instead.

chufei.intro_tr: 除非[chúfēi] means "unless" and introduces the ONE and ONLY condition under which the result in the second clause can happen (or fail to happen). It is a formal, written-style structure typically paired with 才[cái] ("only then") to stress exclusivity, or with 否则[fǒuzé] / 不然[bùrán] ("otherwise") to warn of an unwanted consequence if the condition is not met. Semantically it overlaps heavily with 只有...才 ("only if... then"), but 除非 puts stronger rhetorical emphasis on the exception being rare or hard to fulfill. Word order is flexible: the 除非 clause can open the sentence or follow an initial topic, but the second clause almost always contains 才 or 否则/不然.

tables.caption_tr: Core Sentence Patterns with 除非[chúfēi]
rows: Unless A, only then will B do C
Most common written pattern; stresses A is the sole condition
B states an undesired/negative outcome that will occur if A fails
不然 is the spoken/colloquial equivalent of 否则
Even more colloquial, common in casual conversation
除非[chúfēi] A，否则[fǒuzé] B 就[jiù] C
Unless A, otherwise B will then C
否则 clause can add 就 to link a further consequence

tables.caption_tr: Word Order Options
rows: Topic fronted for emphasis, then 除非 clause
否则/不然 clause always second
否则/不然 clause can never come first; it always states the fallback

tables.caption_tr: 除非 vs Similar 'Unless / Only If' Structures
rows: Formal, emphasizes a rare/strict single exception
除非[chúfēi]下雪[xiàxuě]，否则[fǒuzé]比赛[bǐsài]照常[zhàocháng]举行[jǔxíng]。
Neutral necessary condition, no implied 'otherwise bad outcome'
Simple negative conditional, weaker/less formal than 除非
Refers to a real past/present fact preventing something, not a hypothetical rule

tables.caption_tr: 否则 vs 不然: Formality Comparison
Common Mistakes
rows: Using 除非 without 才 or 否则/不然 in the second clause
除非 needs a paired marker to complete the exclusive-condition meaning
除非[chúfēi]你[nǐ]帮[bāng]我[wǒ]，我[wǒ]才[cái]能[néng]完成[wánchéng]。 (not just 除非你帮我，我能完成)
Putting 否则/不然 clause before 除非 clause
否则/不然 always presents the fallback AFTER the condition is stated
除非[chúfēi] A，否则[fǒuzé] B — never 否则 B，除非 A
Confusing with 如果不 (simple negative if)
除非 implies THE ONLY way, stronger than a plain negative conditional
Use 除非 only when stressing there is no other possible condition
Adding 就 instead of 才 after 除非 clause when meaning 'only if'
就 suggests an easy automatic result, weakening the 'only under this strict condition' nuance
Prefer 才[cái] to keep the exclusive-condition emphasis

jiaru-jiashi.intro_tr: 假如[jiǎrú] and 假使[jiǎshǐ] are the formal, written-style equivalents of English "if / supposing that", used to set up a hypothetical condition. They work exactly like the everyday word 如果[rúguǒ], but carry a bookish, elevated tone that belongs in essays, news reports, speeches, and formal writing rather than casual chat. The second (result) clause is usually introduced by 就[jiù], 那么[nàme], or the very literary 则[zé] to link the hypothesis to its consequence. Between the two, 假如[jiǎrú] is fairly common in formal registers, while 假使[jiǎshǐ] is rarer and even more literary, often felt as slightly old-fashioned. Because both are written-language markers, native speakers almost never use them in relaxed spoken conversation — there, 如果[rúguǒ] or 要是[yàoshi] are preferred instead.

tables.caption_tr: Formality Spectrum of Conditional Words ('if')
rows: Sounds relaxed; avoid in formal essays
Even more bookish than 假如/假使

tables.caption_tr: Basic Sentence Pattern
rows: 假如[jiǎrú] 你 有 时间 ('if you have time')
Placed at the start of the sentence
(你) 就[jiù] 可以 来 ('then you can come')
就/那么/则 is optional but very common
...的话[dehuà] attached after the condition clause
假如 你 有 时间 的话[dehuà] ('if you happen to have time')
Common in speeches; softens the hypothesis

tables.caption_tr: Result-Clause Markers and Their Nuance
rows: 假如下雨,我们就取消比赛。 (Jiǎrú xiàyǔ, wǒmen jiù qǔxiāo bǐsài.)
'Then, in that case' — slightly more formal, often with a pause
假如你不同意,那么我们再商量。 (Jiǎrú nǐ bù tóngyì, nàme wǒmen zài shāngliang.)
Very formal/literary, typical of written argumentation
假如经济下滑,则失业率上升。 (Jiǎrú jīngjì xiàhuá, zé shīyèlǜ shàngshēng.)
假使失败了也不要放弃。 (Jiǎshǐ shībài le yě bú yào fàngqì.)

tables.caption_tr: Common Collocations & Fixed Patterns
rows: 'Suppose that...' — introduces a hypothetical for illustration
假如说我们输了比赛,大家也不要灰心。 (Jiǎrú shuō wǒmen shū le bǐsài, dàjiā yě bú yào huīxīn.)
Softens the hypothesis; common in speeches
假如可以的话,请早点告诉我。 (Jiǎrú kěyǐ dehuà, qǐng zǎodiǎn gàosu wǒ.)
假使遇到困难也不能放弃。 (Jiǎshǐ yùdào kùnnán yě bù néng fàngqì.)
假如不是你帮忙,我们不会成功。 (Jiǎrú búshì nǐ bāngmáng, wǒmen bú huì chénggōng.)

tables.caption_tr: 假如 vs 假使 vs 如果 — Key Differences
footnotes_tr: In real usage, 如果[rúguǒ] can replace 假如[jiǎrú] or 假使[jiǎshǐ] in almost any sentence and sounds natural everywhere; the reverse is not true — using 假如/假使 in casual chat sounds stiff or bookish.
倘若[tǎngruò] and 若[ruò] are even more literary alternatives worth recognizing in reading, though less essential for active production at this stage.

wanyi.intro_tr: 万一[wànyī] introduces a hypothetical situation that the speaker sees as unlikely but wants to prepare for anyway — usually something undesirable, risky, or unwanted. It corresponds to English "in the unlikely event that...", "just in case...", or a worried "what if...?". Unlike neutral conditional words such as 如果[rúguǒ] or 要是[yàoshi], 万一[wànyī] always carries a flavor of low probability and often a negative consequence, which is why it shows up constantly in warnings, backup plans, and anxious questions. It can open a full conditional sentence, stand alone as a short worried question ending in 呢[ne], or act as a noun meaning "mishap/contingency" in fixed phrases like 以防万一[yǐfáng wànyī].

tables.caption_tr: Core Sentence Pattern with 万一[wànyī]
rows: 万一 + Subject + Verb Phrase, (Subject +) 就/也 + Result
万一[wànyī]下雨,我们就[jiù]不去了。
States the unlikely condition first, then the precautionary result
你万一[wànyī]忘了,就[jiù]给我打电话。
Puts focus on the subject before mentioning the risky scenario
万一 + Clause + 的话[dehuà], Result
万一[wànyī]他不同意的话[dehuà],我们再想办法。
Adds a spoken-style pause/softening after the condition
A short worried 'what if...?' question; the result is left unsaid

tables.caption_tr: 万一[wànyī] vs Other Conditional Words
Fixed Expressions Using 万一[wànyī] as a Noun
rows: = 'just in case'; used to justify taking a precaution
refers to something bad/unexpected happening, often about safety or health
wànyī yǒu ge sān cháng liǎng duǎn
'if the worst comes to the worst'
dramatic/formal idiom, usually implies death or serious harm
similar to 以防万一, less commonly heard
footnotes_tr: In these expressions 万一 behaves as a noun meaning 'a small, unlikely chance (of something bad)', not as a conditional conjunction.

tables.caption_tr: Common Adverbs in the Result Clause
rows: 'even so, still' — result holds regardless of the bad scenario
万一失败了,我们也不放弃。
result left implicit in spoken worry-questions ending in 呢

tables.caption_tr: Typical 'Risky Scenario' Collocations with 万一
rows: in case (someone) fails to get in (an exam)

fei-buke.title_tr: 非...不可 (fēi...bùkě): 'Absolutely Must / There's No Choice But To'
fei-buke.intro_tr: 非[fēi]...不可[bùkě] is an emphatic double-negative pattern meaning "absolutely must," "simply have to," or "there's no way around it." Literally, 非 is a literary "if not" and 不可 means "not permissible," so the whole structure says "if this doesn't happen, it's not acceptable" — a very forceful way of expressing necessity. It is more emotional and insistent than the neutral 必须[bìxū], often revealing the speaker's determination, stubbornness, or a strong sense that an outcome is unavoidable (even for predictions like weather). The closing word 不可 can be swapped for the more colloquial 不行[bùxíng] or the old-fashioned 不成[bùchéng] with essentially the same meaning. A separate but related colloquial pattern, 非 + Noun + 不 + (repeated Verb), means "will accept nothing but X" and should not be confused with the "must" pattern covered here.

tables.caption_tr: Core Structure: 非[fēi] + Action/Situation + 不可[bùkě]
rows: opens the structure; sets up the condition
the action or situation that is required
去[qù] 'go', 参加[cānjiā]比赛[bǐsài] 'take part in the competition'
closes the structure, confirms strong necessity
= 'absolutely must VP' / '(Subject) has no choice but to VP'
他[tā]非[fēi]走[zǒu]不可[bùkě]。 'He absolutely must leave.'

tables.caption_tr: Interchangeable Endings for 非...不可
rows: Neutral to formal; most common in writing
你[nǐ]非[fēi]道歉[dàoqiàn]不可[bùkě]。 'You absolutely must apologize.'
Colloquial; very common in daily speech
casual equivalent of 不可, used constantly in conversation
我[wǒ]非[fēi]买[mǎi]不行[bùxíng]。 'I simply have to buy it.'
less common today; found in older or Beijing-flavored speech
这事[zhèshì]非[fēi]他[tā]出面[chūmiàn]不成[bùchéng]。 'This matter absolutely requires him to step in.'

tables.caption_tr: Where the Subject and Topic Can Go
rows: Topic, S + 非[fēi] + VP + 不可[bùkě]
As for this matter, you simply must get involved.

tables.caption_tr: 非...不可 vs Other 'Must' Expressions
rows: emphatic, insistent; speaker's strong will or a sense of inevitability
我[wǒ]非[fēi]赢[yíng]不可[bùkě]。 'I absolutely must win.'
学生[xuéshēng]必须[bìxū]交[jiāo]作业[zuòyè]。 'Students must hand in homework.'
我[wǒ]得[děi]走[zǒu]了[le]。 'I have to go now.'
我[wǒ]一定要[yídìngyào]成功[chénggōng]。 'I am determined to succeed.'

tables.caption_tr: Related Colloquial Pattern: 非 + Noun/Person + 不 + (repeated Verb) — 'will accept nothing but...'
rows: insists on only that thing, refuses anything else
He'll marry no one but you.
footnotes_tr: This pattern looks similar but is grammatically different from 非...不可: here 不 is followed by repeating the SAME verb, not by 可/行/成. Meaning is 'accepts nothing except X', not 'must do X'.

tables.caption_tr: Common Mistakes for Beginners
rows: Using 非[fēi] alone without 不可/不行/不成
非 is a literary negative and sounds incomplete or unnatural without its closing partner
always pair it: 非[fēi]...不可[bùkě] / 不行[bùxíng] / 不成[bùchéng]
Confusing 非...不可 with 除非[chúfēi]...才[cái] ('unless...then')
除非 introduces the ONLY condition under which something happens — a different logical direction from the strong necessity of 非...不可
keep 除非[chúfēi]...才[cái] and 非[fēi]...不可[bùkě] as separate patterns
Placing 不可[bùkě] before the verb
不可 must come at the END of the clause, after the verb or situation described
S + 非[fēi] + VP + 不可[bùkě], never 不可 + VP
Overusing 非...不可 in neutral formal writing
非...不可 carries emotional emphasis or insistence; plain rules and requirements read better with 必须[bìxū]
reserve 非...不可 for emphatic, personal, or inevitable-sounding statements

shifou.intro_tr: 是否[shìfǒu] is the formal, written-style equivalent of 是不是[shìbúshì], meaning "whether (or not)". It shows up constantly in news reports, official documents, surveys, business writing, and academic Chinese, almost always inside an embedded (indirect) question after verbs like 询问[xúnwèn] "to inquire", 讨论[tǎolùn] "to discuss", 决定[juédìng] "to decide", or 确认[quèrèn] "to confirm". Because 是否 already means "whether yes-or-no" by itself, it never takes a following 吗[ma], and it is not combined with a V不V pattern like 去不去[qù bu qù] — that would be redundant. Structurally, 是否 sits right before the verb phrase it questions, and the resulting clause functions as an object clause embedded in a larger sentence rather than as a standalone question. In everyday spoken Chinese, native speakers overwhelmingly prefer 是不是[shìbúshì] or V不V forms; reaching for 是否 signals formality, objectivity, and written register, so it is a strong marker of 书面语[shūmiànyǔ] "written language".

tables.caption_tr: Basic structure: 是否[shìfǒu] + Verb Phrase
rows: Verb (讨论/询问/决定...) + (Subject) + 是否 + VP
我们讨论是否去 [wǒmen tǎolùn shìfǒu qù]
we are discussing whether to go
是否合适，还要考虑 [shìfǒu héshì, hái yào kǎolǜ]
whether it's suitable still needs to be considered
是否 clause as subject of the whole sentence
他是否同意，还不清楚 [tā shìfǒu tóngyì, hái bù qīngchu]
whether he agrees is still unclear

tables.caption_tr: 是否[shìfǒu] vs 是不是[shìbúshì] vs V不V: register comparison
rows: Embedded clauses inside a larger sentence
他是否同意 [tā shìfǒu tóngyì] — "whether he agrees"
Neutral, works in both speech and writing
他是不是同意 [tā shìbúshì tóngyì] — "does he agree or not"
V不V (e.g. 去不去[qù bu qù])
你去不去 [nǐ qù bu qù] — "are you going or not"

tables.caption_tr: Common verb + 是否 collocations
rows: 他还没决定是否参加。[Tā hái méi juédìng shìfǒu cānjiā.] — He hasn't decided whether to take part.
大家在讨论是否涨价。[Dàjiā zài tǎolùn shìfǒu zhǎngjià.] — Everyone is discussing whether to raise the price.
他询问是否还有位子。[Tā xúnwèn shìfǒu hái yǒu wèizi.] — He asked whether there were still seats.
请确认是否收到邮件。[Qǐng quèrèn shìfǒu shōudào yóujiàn.] — Please confirm whether the email was received.
老师检查是否有人缺席。[Lǎoshī jiǎnchá shìfǒu yǒurén quēxí.] — The teacher checked whether anyone was absent.
医生判断是否需要手术。[Yīshēng pànduàn shìfǒu xūyào shǒushù.] — The doctor determines whether surgery is needed.

tables.caption_tr: 是否 + adjective/state: common formal collocations
rows: 消息是否属实尚待证实。[Xiāoxi shìfǒu shǔshí shàng dài zhèngshí.]
请核对答案是否正确。[Qǐng héduì dá'àn shìfǒu zhèngquè.]
这个方案是否合适还需讨论。[Zhège fāng'àn shìfǒu héshì hái xū tǎolùn.]
工程师检查桥梁是否安全。[Gōngchéngshī jiǎnchá qiáoliáng shìfǒu ānquán.]
领导正在评估是否必要加班。[Lǐngdǎo zhèngzài pínggū shìfǒu bìyào jiābān.]

tables.caption_tr: Related formal "whether/or not" words
rows: Formal "whether" before a full verb phrase; most general of this group
他是否来 [tā shìfǒu lái] — "whether he is coming"
Formal version of 能不能[néng bu néng], "whether (one) can"
能否成功还不确定。[Néngfǒu chénggōng hái bú quèdìng.] — "Whether it can succeed is still uncertain."
Very formal, often in polite requests, "whether (one) may"
可否借用一下您的笔？[Kěfǒu jièyòng yíxià nín de bǐ?] — "May I borrow your pen?"
Attached AFTER a word/phrase to mean "or not"; cannot go before the verb
成功与否，取决于努力。[Chénggōng yǔfǒu, qǔjué yú nǔlì.] — "Whether or not one succeeds depends on effort."

tables.caption_tr: Common mistakes with 是否[shìfǒu]
rows: 是否 already expresses the yes/no meaning; adding 吗 is redundant and ungrammatical.
你是否去 [nǐ shìfǒu qù] / 你去不去 [nǐ qù bu qù]
Never combine 是否 with a V不V pattern — pick one, not both.
你是否要喝咖啡？ (in a casual chat with a friend)
你要不要喝咖啡？[nǐ yào bu yào hē kāfēi]
是否 sounds stiff/overly formal in casual spoken conversation; use 要不要 or 是不是 with friends.
是否 used as a standalone question at the end of a sentence: 你同意是否？
是否 must precede the verb phrase it questions, not follow it.

jiang-formal-ba.title_tr: 将 (jiāng): The Formal 把 and the Future-Tense Marker
jiang-formal-ba.intro_tr: 将[jiāng] is a formal, written-register (书面语[shūmiànyǔ]) word with two distinct but related jobs: (1) it works exactly like 把[bǎ], fronting the object before the verb in formal notices, news, rules, and literary writing; and (2) it functions as a marker for future actions, roughly like "will" in English, often paired with 于[yú] to introduce a time or place. Because 将 belongs to written/formal style, you will meet it constantly in news broadcasts, official announcements, contracts, and essays, but it sounds stiff in casual speech, where 把[bǎ] and 要[yào]/会[huì] are used instead. Zero-level learners should first recognize 将 by context (formal writing) before trying to produce it themselves — treat this page as a reading-comprehension and later a writing-upgrade tool.

tables.caption_tr: The two core functions of 将[jiāng] at a glance
rows: will / is going to / is about to

tables.caption_tr: 将 as a formal substitute for 把 — structure comparison
rows: Yes — bare verb alone is ungrammatical
Official notices, laws, news reports, written directives
将 sounds unnatural / overly stiff in casual speech
不 / 没 + 将 (rare; formal writing usually restructures instead)

tables.caption_tr: 将 as a future marker — common patterns
rows: Plain formal future, common in news
中国将举办这次比赛。 (Zhōngguó jiāng jǔbàn zhè cì bǐsài.)
Slightly stronger emphasis on 'about to / going to'
他将要离开这座城市。 (Tā jiāngyào líkāi zhè zuò chéngshì.)
飞机即将起飞。 (Fēijī jíjiāng qǐfēi.)
这个决定将会改变很多人的生活。 (Zhège juédìng jiānghuì gǎibiàn hěn duō rén de shēnghuó.)
Very common in formal announcements to state when/where
展览将于下周开幕。 (Zhǎnlǎn jiāng yú xià zhōu kāimù.)

tables.caption_tr: Set expressions built on 将 — do not translate word-by-word

suo-structure.title_tr: 所 (suǒ) Structure: 所 + Verb, 所谓, 所有
suo-structure.intro_tr: 所 (suǒ) is a classical Chinese element that survives in modern Mandarin mostly in formal writing and a handful of fixed expressions. Placed directly before a verb, 所 turns the verb into a noun-like phrase meaning "that which is [verb]ed", and it is most often seen in the pattern (Subject +) 所 + Verb + 的 + Noun, which builds a relative clause emphasizing the object of the action (this is basically a fancier, more literary version of Verb + 的 + Noun). Outside this core pattern, 所 also shows up frozen inside several very common expressions that you should simply memorize as whole words: 所谓 ("so-called, what is meant by"), 所有 ("all, every"), 有所 + Verb ("to some extent, somewhat" — formal), and the literary passive 为...所... ("to be [verb]ed by"). None of these forms are essential for basic conversation, but they appear constantly in HSK5+ reading passages, news, and essays, so recognizing them is more urgent than being able to produce them fluently.

tables.caption_tr: Overview of Core 所 (suǒ) Patterns
rows: Nominalizes the verb into 'that which is V-ed'; formal/written register
'So-called, what is meant by'; can be neutral (defining a term) or ironic (casting doubt)
所谓专家[suǒwèi zhuānjiā] — 'the so-called expert'
'All, every'; refers to the totality of a set
'To some extent, somewhat'; softens the degree of change or state, formal
Literary passive, equivalent to a formal 被
为大家所知[wéi dàjiā suǒ zhī] — 'known by everyone'

tables.caption_tr: 所 + Verb + 的 + Noun: Building Relative Clauses
rows: the words I said / what I said
the service(s) provided by the company
footnotes_tr: Adding 所 before the verb here is optional and purely stylistic — 我所说的话 and 我说的话 mean the same thing, but the 所 version sounds more formal/literary.
The 的 before the noun is mandatory whenever 所+V modifies a following noun.

tables.caption_tr: 所谓 (suǒwèi) — 'So-called' / 'What Is Meant By'
rows: Defining a term neutrally: 所谓X，就是Y
所谓幸福，就是内心的满足。
Suǒwèi xìngfú, jiù shì nèixīn de mǎnzú.
So-called happiness is simply inner contentment.
Ironic / skeptical tone, casting doubt on the label
所谓的朋友，关键时刻却不见了。
Suǒwèi de péngyou, guānjiàn shíkè què bú jiàn le.
These so-called friends were nowhere to be found when it mattered.
Introducing a term formally before explaining it: 所谓...是指...
所谓通货膨胀，是指物价普遍上涨的现象。
Suǒwèi tōnghuò péngzhàng, shì zhǐ wùjià pǔbiàn shàngzhǎng de xiànxiàng.
What is called inflation refers to the phenomenon of a general rise in prices.

tables.caption_tr: 所有 (suǒyǒu) — 'All / Every'
rows: More formal/written style, common with abstract or collective nouns
More natural in speech; 的 is usually expected before ordinary countable nouns
都 is almost always required when 所有...是主语 subject — omitting 都 sounds incomplete
所有 as a noun on its own ('everything one has')
Tā bǎ suǒyǒu dōu gěi le tā.
Less common; usually appears in set phrases like 一无所有[yìwúsuǒyǒu] 'to have nothing at all'

tables.caption_tr: 有所 + Verb: Common Formal Collocations
rows: to have improved to some extent
to differ somewhat, to be somewhat different
footnotes_tr: 有所 is always followed by a two-syllable verb and is never used in casual spoken sentences — it belongs to news reports, reports, and essays.
有所 cannot take an object directly after the verb; the degree stays vague ('somewhat'), not specific.

rows: Neutral, works in speech and writing
Rarely — the agent is usually stated
Yes — 他被打了 'He got hit' (agent omitted) is fine

所以 (suǒyǐ) — a completely separate word
